💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, last year, Aura released the Aura Ink, its first digital photo frame using an e-ink display rather than the LCD screens common to the other devices that made them the major player in the market (Aura customers have already uploaded more than one billion photos this year alone).
  • Industry observers note that most digital photo frames will remind you of an iPad with a decorative border around it.
  • Now for the downsides: Where most digital frames allow you to flick between photos with a swipe, the Aura Ink is much more sluggish—switching from one photo to another takes about 45 seconds.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, last year, Aura released the Aura Ink, its first digital photo frame using an e-ink display rather than the LCD screens common to the other devices that made them the major player in the market (Aura customers have already uploaded more than one billion photos this year alone). When I reviewed the original 13-inch Aura Ink last year, I recommended it, with a few major reservations. Today, Aura announced its second-generation 10-inch Ink frame, and while I wouldn't exactly say they've solved every one of my issues, the newly introduced device is significantly improved—and much cheaper.

Industry observers note that most digital photo frames will remind you of an iPad with a decorative border around it. They're great for displaying hundreds of your photos with vibrant color, but not everyone loves the look, or the fact that these frames always need to be plugged in. An e-ink frame, on the other hand, uses a variant of the sort of low-power screen you'd find in a Kindle Colorsoft—less bright, but more paperlike, and much closer to the look of a traditionally printed photo.The Aura Ink is a great choice if you want a digital frame that looks more like a "real" photo and doesn't need to be plugged in and doesn't light up like a tablet (though it does have a light, it's really to make up for the fact that color e-ink screens don't reflect light very well, and thus can make your pictures look way too dark without an additional boost). You'll still get all the benefits of an LCD frame like the Aura Aspen, including the ability to load photos from anywhere using the versatile Aura app (you can now even text them directly to the frame), but you'll only need to charge it once every few months.

Now for the downsides: Where most digital frames allow you to flick between photos with a swipe, the Aura Ink is much more sluggish—switching from one photo to another takes about 45 seconds. While an LCD can match the colors in your photo exactly, e-ink uses a "dithering algorithm" to blend tiny pixels together to create the illusion of different hues ("millions" of them, according to Aura). In practice, this means up close, your pictures will look rather grainy, and the colors won't be nearly as bright as what you see on your phone screen.

All of that remarked, the Aura Ink is a great product, provided you know what you're buying, and the newly introduced 10-inch model offers some major upgrades over the 13-inch original released in 2025:.

Recent findings suggest that resolution has been bumped up from 150 ppi to 200 ppi, so your images look more detailed and less grainy. (Though the difference is hard to capture in a photo, I can definitely see the improvement when comparing them side-by-side.).

Instead of the six base colors available on the older frame, the 10-inch Aura Ink blends nine different hues to approximate the colors in your images, offering greater color accuracy and improved contrast.

The transition effect when you move between photos has been updated to look more intentional—like waves of color moving across the screen versus a series of increasingly intense flashes.

It's a heck of a lot cheaper: $349, versus $499 for the 13-inch model—though that's still significantly pricier than Aura's most popular offering, the 10.1-inch Aura Carver, which starts around $200 less.

I write a lot about e-ink devices, from e-readers to tablets, and my common refrain, especially with color devices, is that they're great at what they do, but you should understand what they do before you plunk down your money. The Aura Ink will never look as bright and colorful as an LCD frame, and if you want a frame that can switch between images every few minutes or even play video, you'll need to look elsewhere (to maximize battery life, Aura recommends swapping photos on the Aura Ink no more than 12 times per day).

But if you want to display photos that look more like the ones that hung on the walls of your childhood home, in a frame that doesn't need to be plugged in all the time, you'll probably dig it, provided you can stomach the $350 price tag.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Hulu's long-promised integration with Disney+ is nigh.

Sources indicate that the subscription streaming platform has a robust library of original content, including the Emmy-winning dystopian drama The Handmaid's Tale, the mega-popular comedy whodunit Only Murders in the Building, the Predator prequel Prey, and the 2022 horror reboot Hellraiser, as well as prestige series from FX on Hulu such as The Bear and Shōgun. Disney acquired a majority stake in Hulu in 2019 and closed deals to acquire the other ownership interests in 2025. Since 2024, they have been integrating Hulu content more and more into the proprietary service Disney+ while maintaining both platforms as largely separate entities in the U.S.

According to recent reports, they added that "we are also adding more vertical video, live sports and podcasts to the [Disney+] platform, while continuing to explore other emerging content genres.” In December, this will include content from TikTok creators that is "strategically aligned" with the release of the upcoming Avengers: Doomsday on December 18. This is part of Disney's recent deal with the social video platform.

Avengers: Doomsday is the first Avengers teamup film in the Marvel Cinematic Universe since 2019's Avengers: Endgame, which is the highest-grossing movie of all time.

In a recent development, the addition of more vertical content to Disney+ is part of a content expansion blueprint that has been taking place for some time. In 2026, they launched a series of Locker Diaries shorts, which followed interactions between characters from some of their most popular brands, as viewed from inside an open locker in a school hallway (thus mimicking the typical vertical frame of a TikTok video). This series included characters from across the Disney+ spectrum, including the musical franchises Z-O-M-B-I-E-S, Camp Rock, and Descendants, the animated series Phineas and Ferb, and the upcoming supernatural teen drama Coven Academy.

There is some amount of overlap between the casts of the Locker Diaries shorts, particularly when it comes to Malachi Barton, who plays characters in Z-O-M-B-I-E-S, Camp Rock, and Coven Academy. Below, see a breakdown of the actors who play multiple characters in the vertical series:.

It ultimately remains to be seen if and when Hulu folds entirely into Disney+ in the United States. However, that is the only major region where it is still a standalone service. 💡 Key Takeaways
  • Many phrases come to mind when thinking of The Witcher series: dark, unforgiving, morally ambiguous, Geralt in a bathtub.
  • In an article from the 25th anniversary Xbox Magazine, CD Projekt Red staff shared newly introduced details about the long-awaited 2027 add-on to The Witcher 3.
  • Letten is inspired by Polish romantic poetry, the English countryside, Tudor architecture, and some of the more verdant areas in the original Witcher game.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Many phrases come to mind when thinking of The Witcher series: dark, unforgiving, morally ambiguous, Geralt in a bathtub. According to The Witcher 3’s latest DLC Songs of the Past principal writer, Alexandra Motyka, this new chapter in Geralt's saga will add a few new adjectives to that list: “We wanted it to be paced differently from other adventures — a slow burn, sentimental, and somehow soothing.”.

In an article from the 25th anniversary Xbox Magazine, CD Projekt Red staff shared newly introduced details about the long-awaited 2027 add-on to The Witcher 3. We already knew the story would take place in Letten, an unexplored region of The Witcher’s world and Dandelion’s ancestral home, but the interview gives more context on the specific vibe and atmosphere the team is going for with this new locale.

Letten is inspired by Polish romantic poetry, the English countryside, Tudor architecture, and some of the more verdant areas in the original Witcher game. It will be new territory for The Witcher series at large, as the author of the books, Andrzej Sapkowski, never explored the area in his works. “Uncovering a new region on the map of The Witcher world is just as thrilling for us as for the players,” Motyka said. “This time we could use our creative freedom while still remaining within the boundaries of the imaginary world we inherited.”.

The Xbox Magazine article adds that while Letten is a much more outwardly idyllic place than most backdrops in the series, there will still be monsters to fight and dark secrets to uncover. However, one of the main reasons for this adventure is to return to beloved characters, like Dandelion.

“We could have chosen any reason to set off on a latest journey — but all of us wanted it to be about Dandelion," CD Projekt Red narrative director Philipp Weber said. "He is a very much loved character and his bond with Geralt was always touching. We shove the characters into new, challenging situations, we make it tough for them, in order to shift the dynamics of their relationship and show its depth.”.

The interview also confirms that Songs of the Past takes place after the events ot The Witcher 3: Blood and Wine. “We always stated that Geralt deserved his rest after Blood and Wine, and we stick by that," Weber said. "However, that doesn’t mean that Geralt can never go on an adventure again, especially with his best friend…”.

Beyond 2027’s Songs of the Past, CD Projekt Red has already announced that The Witcher 4 is planned for a 2028 release window. CD Projekt Red’s CEO, Michał Nowakowski, previously remarked that he wants the studio to release a full trilogy of Witcher games over six years. It’s quite an ambitious plan, one that subverts the extended timelines many AAA games face these days. If that wasn’t enough, CD Projekt Red has many other projects in development: a remake of the original Witcher game, a multiplayer Witcher title, a Cyberpunk 2077 sequel, and an unnamed fresh IP, Project Hadar.

Now, in Ludwig, he takes on another socially awkward, semi-reclusive character, but John Taylor has a much more productive way of putting his obsession to use. Under the pseudonym Ludwig, John is an acclaimed puzzle setter whose methodical mind and extraordinary ability to recognize patterns also happen to make him excellent at solving murders.

Industry observers note that that talent might have remained undiscovered if it weren't for his sister-in-law Lucy (Anna Maxwell Martin), who forces the reluctant John into impersonating his twin brother, a DCI in the local police force, after he mysteriously disappears. The mystery surrounding James' whereabouts continues into Season 2, but John no longer has to hide behind his brother's identity in this “soft murder” take on The Parent Trap. Instead, the Cambridge Police Authority has brought him in as a "Crime Consultant".

With the second season having just finished its run on BritBox, Ludwig executive producer Kenton Allen joins Collider to discuss the series' success, the challenges of continuing the same story with a fresh dynamic, and why comedy actors seem so well suited to murder mysteries. He also discusses whether Ludwig could become a long-running detective franchise, teases the series' Christmas special featuring Poirot himself, David Suchet, and shares what audiences can expect from Rabbit, the U.S. adaptation currently being developed by Humphrey Ker (Welcome to Wrexham) and Megan Ganz (It's Always Sunny in Philadelphia).

ALLEN: So he rang me and said, "I've got a secret I need to tell you." I'm slightly worrying what that secret might be. And his secret was he wanted to play a TV detective. I suppose that David, I sort of have this firm belief that the really great actors, particularly in this sort of genre, have come through half-hour comedy. And so if you look at British TV and you think of things like Cracker — Robbie Coltrane, I know Cracker wasn't a detective, but he sort of was — and you think of Alan Davies and Jonathan Creek, and Alan Davies came through 30-minute TV, and you think of David Jason and A Touch of Frost, and there's a great lineage of comedy half-hour sitcom actors stepping up into one hour. Some people call them “cozy crime,” a phrase I don't like. We prefer “soft murder.”.

It has been revealed that ALLEN: Yeah. Well, you need an actor that can play that, you know, that can do the serious business of investigating murders, but can also bring the charm and the wit and the irreverence to it. And I think that David brings that to Ludwig, and he has a light element to David in his real life, which I tease him about regularly.

I think he sort of embodies who Ludwig is, which is an outsider, a loner, somebody who prefers his own company to the company of other people, somebody who's very clever but is also quite shy, et cetera, et cetera.

I was intrigued by that connection between comedy and drama. So you mentioned the example of Alan Davies, David Jason, and there's also been a lot of talk around, perhaps this year especially — I went to the Edinburgh TV Festival, and they were all talking about how comedy, British comedy, has this huge resurgence. ALLEN: I don't think it's comedy, really, that brings something to the genre, but I think that in these sort of shows, these sort of murder-of-the-week shows, I think that in a world which is increasingly confusing and upsetting and there doesn't seem to be any answers to anything, I think spending an hour with somebody who is clever and entertaining and fallible and has all sorts of complications, but is capable of sorting out a whodunnit in 60 minutes, is rather reassuring.

There is some order in the world. Puzzles do get solved. Bad people do get caught. I think it's to do with that. I think the comedy, I think people, I think there's a bit of weariness about very hard murder shows. Some American television executive once described to me, "dead women in the trunk of a car" show, which is not a genre of television.

I think escaping into a world where problems get solved, but we don't focus too much on the grisliness of the murder and focus more on the how was it done and who did it, I think there's some comfort in that. In a recent development, the same there is in Traitors, when you're watching them get murdered, but they're not actually getting murdered. That first season, we had that added tension of John impersonating James and when was everybody going to find out, and then everybody found that out at the end of the first season.

So, you've got to come back to Ludwig in a sort of upcoming dynamic in a different way. How can he still be involved with the police investigations in this new season? How did you ensure that this second series maintained that same level of suspense, and how did it keep audiences just as gripped?

ALLEN: Yeah. Well, I think the blueprint was always, from day one of developing the show, that Ludwig could only pretend to be his brother for one season because I think it stretches credibility to think that he could get away with that for more than a couple of weeks. 💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that throughout his 64 years in movies, James Bond, the hard-living superspy, has been the star of the 007 franchise. But by granting Robert Pattinson a license to kill, the producers of the next Bond film are making a bet that one of the most famous men on the planet can slide into a role shaped by the likes of Sean Connery, Daniel Craig, Roger Moore, and Pierce Brosnan without bringing any Edward Cullen-sized baggage.

Sources indicate that it’s quite a gamble. After all, Connery, Craig, Timothy Dalton, and poor, delusional George Lazenby were relative unknowns when they were tapped to play the secret agent, and Brosnan and Moore were TV-famous but unproven as film stars. That’s not the case with Pattinson, who has been one of the most recognizable people on the planet for two decades, and who is at the moment anchoring another massive franchise in “Batman.” So why did director Denis Villeneuve, producers David Heyman and Amy Pascal, and Amazon MGM Studios decide to hand over the keys to the Aston Martin to such a prominent and expensive candidate? Related Stories ‘The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth’ First Reactions: Quentin Tarantino and David Fincher Deliver a ‘Pure Riot’ of a Hangout Movie ‘Hershey’ Review: An Unbelievably Flavorless Biopic About America’s Most Famous Chocolatier.

Well, some of it has to do with Villeneuve’s comfort level. He’s worked with Pattinson on “Dune: Part Three” and knows what the mercurial star can bring to a role. Clearly, he wants to build a darker, brooding Bond. Then, there’s also the need to have insurance. Amazon is launching a new iteration of 007 into a world that looks very different than it did in 2019 when the last chapter, “No Time to Die,” was conceived and shot (it wouldn’t be released until 2021 thanks to COVID). We’ve lived through #MeToo, a pandemic, wars in Ukraine and the Middle East, the fraying of the Western World and, with it, the “special relationship” Bond has sworn to protect. From the start, Amazon was interested in picking a higher-profile actor to outfit in one of Bond’s signature tuxedos. Before the search began in earnest last May, executives were high on the idea of Jacob Elordi.

Plus, some of the other finalists, a group that included Callum Turner, Jack Lowden, Josh O’Connor, and Nicholas Hoult, lacked the kind of sex appeal and danger that the part required. Hoult apparently impressed executives with his audition, but came up short, as he did when he was in contention for Batman (losing out to Pattinson) and Superman (getting Lex Luthor as a consolation prize). He remains very well liked in the industry. With a salary estimated at roughly $2.5 million, Hoult would have been a cheaper option than Pattinson, who one industry source speculated would cost north of $10 million to hire.

But the higher price tag may be worth it. This isn’t just the first Bond to be released under Amazon’s ownership — it’s the first to be produced without the Broccoli family at the helm. The keepers of the 007 flame sold their creative control to Amazon in 2025, leaving the series without a guiding force. Both Heyman and Pascal are old hands, having overseen the casting of the Harry Potter and Spider-Man franchises, respectively, but those are still substantial shoes to fill.

Recent findings suggest that what’s in it for Pattinson? Well, a chance to put his stamp on an iconic role, as well as an opportunity to reunite with Villeneuve, one of the hottest directors in Hollywood. His commercial bona fides have also, arguably, never been higher. Not only has he shown he can anchor a superhero film with “The Batman” and its upcoming sequel, but he’s also opened more idiosyncratic fare, such as the recent A24 hits “The Drama” and “Primetime.” Clearly, he can bring in the younger audiences driving the box office turnaround while retaining a kind of indie cool that could take Bond in a fresh and exciting direction. Will he be our perviest 007?

In a recent development, plus, the recent shake-up at DC Studios, with James Gunn and Peter Safran replaced by former Marvel executive Jeremy Latcham, may spell trouble for Matt Reeves’ “The Batman” series. Although it was conceived as a trilogy, the sequel was delayed multiple times as Reeves dealt with personal matters, forcing him to leave production last month, with Steven Soderbergh stepping in to finish shooting. DC may not want to wait as long to make another installment, and there’s a sense that Latcham may want something brighter and more mainstream than Reeves’ moody, hard PG-13 take on The Dark Knight.

It has been revealed that but Pattinson better get ready for a lot more scrutiny than the questions that greeted his casting as Bruce Wayne. “With Batman, there’s a mask to hide behind,” mentioned one industry source. “With Bond, your face is front and center.”.

Even Craig, widely considered to be the best Bond since Connery, faced fierce blowback when his casting was revealed. He was too blonde, too unconventionally handsome. A website, CraigNotBond, sprang up where fans vented their displeasure.

According to recent reports, but when “Casino Royale” debuted in 2006, and Craig demonstrated that he was perfectly capable of kicking ass and ordering his martini shaken, not stirred, the haters were swiftly silenced. Will Pattinson be able to pull off the same stunt? It’s a high-risk, high-reward gamble. Just the kind of bet James Bond lives to make.

'GTA 6' Runs Best on This Console

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (694 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Grand Theft Auto 6 might just be the most anticipated game of all time.
  • Recent findings suggest that now, few of us will buy a game console specifically for GTA 6—unless you don't already have a current-generation PlayStation or Xbox.
  • In a recent development, rockstar confirmed as much in a post on Tuesday, which was meant to spread the news about pre-loading the game.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6 might just be the most anticipated game of all time. It's been 13 years since Rockstar dropped GTA 5, and after years of rumors, leaks, and official announcements, the sixth mainstream installment in the series is nearly here. In fact, anyone who pre-ordered the game digitally can now pre-load it onto their console, if you want to ensure you're ready to play the second the game comes out.

Recent findings suggest that now, few of us will buy a game console specifically for GTA 6—unless you don't already have a current-generation PlayStation or Xbox. (The PC version of the game isn't expected until at least early 2027.) But, as it turns out, there's one specific console that can run GTA 6 better than the rest.

In a recent development, rockstar confirmed as much in a post on Tuesday, which was meant to spread the news about pre-loading the game. But, interestingly, it spurred a discussion about the performance of the game itself, as well as which consoles are best to run it.

No matter which console you play GTA 6 on, Rockstar says that the game will only target 30 fps (frames per second). That's decided slow for a mainstream game in 2026. GTA 5 also shipped at 30 fps in 2013, but newer consoles can run it at higher frame rates. In fact, most games that launch on the latest generation of consoles can run at 60 fps, if not higher. While it's certainly not a dealbreaker, it is interesting that Rockstar's latest game can't run at a faster frame rate even on the PS5 Pro or the Xbox Series X.

To that point, Rockstar called out the PS5 Pro specifically in its post, announcing, "The PlayStation 5 Pro offers breathtaking visuals, with improved clarity through PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR) and ray-traced shadows only available on PlayStation 5 Pro.".

Sources indicate that PSSR is Sony's AI upscaler, similar to options like DLSS from Nvidia, which uses AI to add extra graphical information to games in real time. That allows developers like Rockstar to run the game at a lower resolution to save on processing power, but still boost the visuals to reach a higher perceived resolution. As such, it's not as ideal as running the game at a higher resolution natively, but it can help improve the visuals without pushing the hardware beyond its limits. Meanwhile, ray-tracing offers realistic lighting effects and can also be graphically intense.

While PlayStation and Xbox players alike will be stuck at 30 fps, it seems only PS5 Pro gamers will be able to play the game with ray-tracing effects and AI upscaling. It's surprising that Xbox Series X players don't have similar benefits, as the hardware is more powerful than Xbox Series S. Rockstar didn't specify why only the PS5 Pro gets these upgrades.

In the post, Rockstar also announced that the PS5 version of GTA 6 takes advantage of other PlayStation-exclusive perks, like high-fidelity haptic feedback in the DualSense controller, spatial audio rendering using the PlayStation's Tempest 3D audio, as well as improved load times—though Rockstar didn't specify what those load times would be. These perks apply to all PS5 consoles, not just PS5 Pros. Rockstar goes so far as to say that GTA 6 plays best on PlayStation 5 consoles.

That's not to say that Microsoft's consoles are totally left out of the perks. Rockstar claims that GTA 6 will be available on Xbox Cloud Gaming on both Xbox Series X and S, as well as Xbox One. In addition, both PlayStation and Xbox gamers can play GTA 6 using Remote Play, so no one has to physically play on their console if they want to game on the go.

In a recent development, again, there's no reason to go out and buy a specific console for GTA 6, so long as you have something that can run the game. After all, PS5 Pros are difficult to find, especially without wildly overpaying. But it's interesting that Rockstar has managed to give Sony's consoles the extra perks here, particularly since the firm hasn't explained why that is.

Sources indicate that the one I’ve been testing the most is Apple Notes. Siri has offered basic Notes-related functionality for years, but it gains a whole new set of powers with the new update.

Here’s everything Siri told me it can do in Notes as of iOS 27.3:.

That’s a lot of capabilities that can all now be handled by Siri.

Magic: The Gathering’s Newly introduced Commander Decks Offer Less for the Same Price

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (880 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Polygon

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Magic: The Gathering players know it's an expensive hobby.
  • Recent findings suggest that during MagicCon: Atlanta 2026, Wizards of the Coast officially presented Magic's latest set in a dedicated showcase, and I'm not talking about Star Trek, which saw its global launch that very weekend.
  • In a recent development, however, there is still a chance to get those fancy borderless Commander cards.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Magic: The Gathering players know it's an expensive hobby. Whether you're trying to keep up with a rapidly changing Standard format or you just want to add a spicy latest card to your Commander deck, the hobby has surely gotten progressively more expensive. However, it's one thing to see product prices rise, and a completely different one to see that product lose some of its features while keeping the same price.

Recent findings suggest that during MagicCon: Atlanta 2026, Wizards of the Coast officially presented Magic's latest set in a dedicated showcase, and I'm not talking about Star Trek, which saw its global launch that very weekend. Nauctis: The Sunken Realm is the next in-universe Magic set, scheduled for release on Feb. 5, 2027. Nauctis will introduce a brand-latest, underwater world, and the set will feature a variety of products, as usual. This includes four Commander decks, but players have noticed that borderless Commander cards will no longer be included in the product, which is still being sold at a retail price of $49.99.

In a recent development, however, there is still a chance to get those fancy borderless Commander cards. The Premium Edition Commander Decks include one foil borderless face Commander and one foil borderless featured Commander. Plus, the entire deck is foil. However, the retail price for Premium Edition decks is $79.99. This means that players who really like having their borderless Commanders will have to shell out more money than usual, even if that comes with a full foil deck.

That's not the only controversial change that Nauctis will bring to Magic products. Starting with this set, Collector Boosters will drop from 15 cards to 12, while Standard Bundles will no longer feature foil full art lands, and the number of foil basic lands will drop from 15 to 10. Wizards of the Coast explained the reasoning behind some of the changes to make room for various printing experiments like God Packs, but many fans are understandably unhappy.

According to recent reports, nonetheless, the Nauctis Commander Decks at least seem exciting. The Boros (red-white) Seal the Deal has perhaps the best deck name in Magic history. The Bant (white-blue-green) Merfolk Regiment will add more options to one of the most popular typal decks in Magic. Izzet (blue-red) Blood in the Water has sharks. Need I say more? Finally, Sultai (green-blue-black) Terrors of the Abyss looks like the strongest option, if only because its two Commanders, the Ignoble Serpent and Zekes, Acid Rock Fan, have already been inadvertently spoiled on Scryfall.

Recent findings suggest that terrors of the Abyss's box features the phrases "discard and mill" and "reanimate sea monsters," and that seems to be a strong strategy, based on the deck's Commanders. The Ignoble Serpent costs eight mana (five colorless, one green, one blue, one black) for a 7/9 legendary serpent noble. Its text box reads:.

At the beginning of your first upkeep in this game, if The Ignoble Serpent is in your command zone, mill four cards.

Industry observers note that at the beginning of your end step, return target sea monster creature card from your graveyard to the battlefield. (Krakens, Leviathans, Octopuses, Serpents, and Whales are sea monsters.).

It has been revealed that commander players know how powerful passive abilities that activate while a Commander is in the Command Zone are, thanks to the infamous Eminence ability. This serpent starts its engine right away on turn one. If you can mill a powerful sea monster in the first four cards of your deck, then as soon as you play The Ignoble Serpent later in the game, that sea monster can hit the battlefield for free. And if you spend most of the game filling up your graveyard with other powerful sea monsters, then Ignoble Serpent's bottom ability makes it fairly easy to overwhelm opponents.

It has been revealed that some of my favorite picks for sea creatures to include in a deck like this would be the classic Simic Sky Swallower (featuring protection and evasion), The Terror of Serpent's Pass, the Unagi of Kiyoshi Island (which provides card draw). I'd be remiss not mentioning the terrific duo of Koma, Cosmos Serpent and Koma, World-Eater, two massive threats that are resilient to removal and also generate a scary number of creature tokens.

However, my favorite option is Sin, Spira's Punishment. When Sin enters or attacks, it makes a copy of another permanent in your graveyard. This means you could get two major monsters on the battlefield for the price of one. Sin can also make copies of lands, and it even draws a card in the process.

With 40 sea monsters in your deck, you have an 89% chance of milling one as part of those first four cards, but since it'll take you awhile to actually get The Ignoble Serpent onto the board, you have time to mill and/or discard sea monsters with cheap effects like Dark Matter Manipulator, Dream Twist, or Mental Note to ensure a major monster hits the battlefield every turn.

Overall, The Ignoble Serpent looks like a hugely powerful Commander, but not necessarily one that's overly game-breaking. Its viability will rely on a careful balance of ramp, mill, discard, and a big pile of nasty sea creatures.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • A lot is happening in front of the camera in “Wildwood” — the general Millennial chaos of Portland, Oregon, swarms of baby-napping crows, an army of wolves with cannons and trebuchets — and just as much behind the camera in Laika Studios’ latest stop-motion epic.

  • According to recent reports, “Back in the old days, like the Ray Harryhausen days — it was still the same as how we do it: You have a puppet; you have an object; you move it a tiny bit; you take a picture; you move it a little more; you take another picture.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A lot is happening in front of the camera in “Wildwood” — the general Millennial chaos of Portland, Oregon, swarms of baby-napping crows, an army of wolves with cannons and trebuchets — and just as much behind the camera in Laika Studios’ latest stop-motion epic. But for all the innovation and blending of CG and stop-motion required to tell the story of Prue McKeel’s (Peyton Elizabeth Lee) impossible quest into the impassable woods, some key tools have stayed the same for Laika since “Coraline.”.

Recent findings suggest that one such tool is Dragonframe, the frame-grabbing software developed by Jamie and Dyami Caliri in 2008, and essential to helping Laika animators craft the naturalistic performances that “Wildwood” director Travis Knight wanted to create. Related Stories Fall Festival Movies Sold: ‘Edward Noted: Between Worlds’ About Palestinian-American Author Lands at Kino Lorber Why Casting Robert Pattinson as James Bond Is a High-Risk, High-Reward Gamble for Denis Villeneuve.

According to recent reports, “Back in the old days, like the Ray Harryhausen days — it was still the same as how we do it: You have a puppet; you have an object; you move it a tiny bit; you take a picture; you move it a little more; you take another picture. But you had no way of knowing exactly what the frame that you just took looked like and how it related to the frame that you’re about to take,” Knight explained on an episode of the Filmmaker Toolkit Podcast. “You had these gauges where you could try to approximate the distance something moved, but it was this act of faith. You didn’t really know; you had to wait until you developed the film to see how it moved. And that’s why a lot of early animation has that kind of herky-jerky quality.”.

Dragonframe and other frame-grabbing software systems take a lot of the guesswork, if not quite all of the faith, out of that process. Laika animators can check what they’ve just done on a computer, moving between the most recent frames taken and the one that an animator is at the moment on. This allows animators to ensure that whatever motion they’re puppeting, be it walking, running, flying, or the unfathomable wrath of nature flowing out through a giant tower of living vines exploding forth from the Earth, flows together.

“Whether it’s a 20-frame shot or a 1000-frame shot, you can look at all the frames that precede it to make sure that the object or the puppet is moving the way it should,” Knight told IndieWire.

Laika has used Dragonframe on every one of its films, but just because a tool is that useful and reliable doesn’t take the artistry and effort of animating out of the equation, or lower the particular stakes of stop-motion.

“2D animation, CG animation, they’re iterative. You can set key frames. You do your breakdowns. You do your in-betweens. You can go back and refine and keep going and reworking things until you get the perfect performance. With stop-motion, it’s progressive. You start on frame one, and the animator, coaxing life with their hands into this puppet, is working their way through a frame at a time. You don’t get to go back and change it.”.

That lack of take-backs permanence, though, also helps stop-motion animators be intentional and certain in their choices. “You’re contorting your body into all these positions to get these puppets to move properly. It’s mentally very draining because you have to do all this three-dimensional chess as you’re trying to figure things out, because it is technical, but it always has to feel organic,” Knight stated. “ It’s human ingenuity, it’s human creativity, it’s devotion, it’s care, it’s time.”.

All that care and time goes into pulling off the magic trick of making steel, silicon, and fabric objects feel fully alive. That’s been the game for stop-motion since Ray Harryhausen. Whenever Laika develops newly introduced processes or sticks with tried-and-true tools, it’s to give animators the ability to do that. “[We don’t want] to get in the way of seeing this puppet as a person. The finest stop-motion animators can do all that with their hands. But we’ve developed different techniques and tools where some of the less experienced animators can actually get to that same level,” Knight stated.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Welcome to Holiday Office Hours From the Labs, a collaborative multimedia project in which Lifehacker, CNET, ZDNET, and Mashable harness the power of our product testing laboratory and our editors' expertise to offer the best gift-buying recommendations possible. In this episode, we're talking televisions.

I recently did a deep dive into TV development history, checked out what was on shelves for 2026, and I concluded that the best gift TV you can give this year is, actually, a pair of sunglasses. The XBX by XReal video display glasses are basically a TV you can shove in your pocket. Check them out:.

Industry observers note that I looked past traditional sets for a couple of reasons. First, because as much as we all love a great show or movie, who actually buys someone a TV set as a gift? More importantly, there's the nature of television itself. Since it was invented in the late 1920s, television quality has been measured by how significant the screen is and how clear and bright the picture is, but in 2026, a nothing-special 4K television delivers an image that is pixel-invisible to a typical viewer, and most of us don't have living rooms big enough to need a display bigger than 65 inches. I think the innovation in the space is going to come from the form factor and the use case, and what better form factor is there than a pair of sunglasses?

These glasses deliver the equivalent of a 142" TV viewed from across the room. It's hard to compare resolution to traditional TVs—technically, the display is 1080p in each eye, but because the TV is just millimeters from your eye, it looks much clearer than that. The peak brightness is 1,600 nits, bright enough for most rooms, and there's a totally opaque shield if you need it. The refresh rate is a crisp 120Hz. They support HDR10 and real-time SDR-to-HDR upscaling, offer billions of colors, and it's all in a package that weighs only 62 grams.

Then there are the use cases. It can act as a separate monitor for your computer; you can watch a different show than your roommate without bothering them; but most of all, these are great for flights. There is no situation in life that calls for a big screen TV more than a cross-country airplane flight. Slip these on with a pair of headphones, and you can fly to Boise in your own private, virtual theater.

They plug right into any device that supports USB-C video, there's no battery to remember to charge, and they cost less than $300. In other words: They're the perfect TV gift for the holidays, even if they aren't technically a TV.

Prime Video's most divisive fantasy release of the year arrived less than a week ago, and its four-episode premiere has already propelled the series to the top of the streaming charts. Set five years after Season 2, The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power Season 3 explores the height of the war between the Elves and the Dark Lord Sauron. The season is set to run through November 25, making it Prime Video's final fantasy release of the year. As a result, no other original fantasy titles will debut on the streamer this year, including one of its most underrated.

Sources indicate that set in the fantasy universe of The Legend of Vox Machina, this series takes place about 20 years later, though you don't need to watch The Legend of Vox Machina to follow it. Titled The Mighty Nein, it centers on a completely different, independent group of outcasts and morally grey characters, adapted from Critical Role's second tabletop campaign. Now, one year after its memorable Season 1 finale, the animated series has finally gotten a Season 2 premiere date, giving fans plenty to look forward to as they return to Exandria.

Industry observers note that unfortunately, The Mighty Nein won't return this year. According to TV Insider, the award-winning series will officially return for its second season on March 24, 2027, with all eight latest episodes dropping at once. The news was revealed on November 15, 2026, during TwitchCon and a special actual-play one-shot titled The Rings of Power: A Middle-Earth One-Shot. The event featured Critical Role cast members Sam Riegel, Travis Willingham, and Liam O'Brien, along with Rings of Power cast members Maxim Baldry and Benjamin Walker. O'Brien, the one-shot's game master, announced the Season 2 release date.

The Mighty Nein Season 2 will bring fan-favorite characters exciting latest adventures. One is a pirate adventure that takes the group across the high seas, where they continue to grapple with their pasts and relationships. The Beacon remains a threat, of course, and longtime Critters familiar with the original Mighty Nein tabletop campaign can expect appearances from new faces.

As fans recall, at the end of The Mighty Nein Season 1, audiences finally saw the misfit antiheroes together for the first time. This included tiefling Jester Lavorre (Laura Bailey), half-orc warlock Fjord Stone (Willingham), goblin Nott the Brave (Riegel), wizard Caleb (O'Brien), Cobalt Soul monk Beauregard Lionett (Marisha Ray), and tiefling bloodhunter Mollymauk Tealeaf (Taliesin Jaffe), all of whom met up with barbarian/mercenary Yasha Nydoorin (Ashley Johnson).

It has been revealed that the Mighty Nein Season 2 premieres in March. Stream past episodes on Prime Video.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Apple continues to expand the appeal of its free Sports app, which focuses on delivering real-time sports scores and stats, across many different sports.

Today, Apple is adding UFC into the mix, so MMA fans can track the fights live through the unified Apple Sports experience.

Apple Sports will provide coverage of every bout across the full fight card, with live stats like total strike counts, takedowns, knockdowns and more.

Apple Sports features animated background artwork to differentiate different games and matches in the detail view, and UFC is no different with a custom backdrop that evokes the ambience of being under the lights of the Octagon. The details card also includes new visualization to illustrate the number of recorded strikes by target.

You can keep up with the action inside the app, or tap the clock icon to start a Live Activity and get score updates delivered directly to your iPhone’s lock screen.

Apple Sports now comes preinstalled when setting up a latest iPhone from scratch. If you don’t already have it, you can get it as a free download from the App Store.

According to recent reports, the Sports app is still only available on iPhone right now though; Apple has still not unveiled plans to do an iPad and Mac native version. You can have the Sports Live Activities from your iPhone show up on Apple Watch and Mac, however.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • 25, Prime Video will release the final two episodes of Lord of the Rings: Rings of Power's third season.
  • According to recent reports, the show's official X account declared this on Nov.
  • This isn't the first time Amazon has brought one of its original Prime Video series to the massive screen, as The Boys' finale also received the treatment earlier this year.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

On Nov. 25, Prime Video will release the final two episodes of Lord of the Rings: Rings of Power's third season. The penultimate episode is already confirmed to depict one of the most key moments in Middle-earth's history, the forging of the One Ring. To give that moment the respect it deserves, the episode is getting a theatrical release.

According to recent reports, the show's official X account declared this on Nov. 16, sharing a link where fans can find local theaters with screenings. As an added bonus, the cinematic event will actually be an early release of season 3's episode 7, as the screenings will take place on Nov. 23 and 24.

This isn't the first time Amazon has brought one of its original Prime Video series to the massive screen, as The Boys' finale also received the treatment earlier this year. As for the actual conclusion to season 3, fans will have to be satisfied seeing that on their TV, phones, or tablets.

Since the start of season 3, audiences have been waiting for Sauron to forge the One Ring. The season, which began with a five-year time jump that serves as a soft reboot of the show, has heavily focused on the villain's attempts to finally create his all-powerful weapon. His failure to do so up to this point has largely been due to the lack of help from the Elven smith Celebrimbor, who forged the rings of power for the dwarves, men, and elves.

In a recent development, the One Ring is arguably the most crucial object in all of Middle-earth, as it features in Tolkien's novel The Hobbit as well as being the main McGuffin of the original Lord of the Rings trilogy. While we've caught glimpses of its forging in Peter Jackson's films, Rings of Power will be the first time we've seen the entire process in all its glory. If you don't mind the changes the show made to the source material, then this will surely be a moment worth seeing on the biggest screen you can find.

From managing your Gmail inbox to downloading apps on your Android phone, pretty much every aspect of your digital life has a little bit of Google in it. That is a lot of power in the hands of a company that makes money by selling your data to advertisers. While you can't fully escape Google's tracking without quitting a whole bunch of essential online services, you can use these privacy hacks to reduce how the company tracks you, as well as protect the information in your Google account.

Your Gmail account doesn't just have one email address. In fact, it has unlimited addresses, but you need a hack to utilize them. When you're signing up for a newly introduced service, you can add another word to your email address, as well as the "+" symbol, to create an alias. For example, if your email is "[email protected]," and you're signing up for an Amazon account, you can use "[email protected]" as your email address. The email will still end up in your main inbox, as if you simply used [email protected]. Not only can this trick turn one Gmail address into an unlimited number of addresses, but it also helps you identify who sold your email address to spammers, because those emails will have the alias in the "To" field.

According to recent reports, if you wish to make your emails more private, you can also link your Proton Mail account to Gmail. This lets you send and receive emails via your Gmail address, while using Proton Mail's privacy protections such as blocking email trackers.

Google wants to show you personalized search results, which initially feels very helpful, but it also ends up trapping you in an algorithmic bubble. The best way to break out of your search bubble is to periodically use other search engines, but if you wish to stick to Google, you can disable personalized search recommendations in Google Search and the Play Store on Android. Go to this settings page, and turn off Personalized Recommendations and Play Personalization.

Google tracks your web and app activity by default, which includes your search history, voice data (if you use the speak-to-search feature), and activity from sites, apps, and devices that use Google services. However, associated information, such as your location data, is also saved to your Google profile, which you might not assume gets included in "Web & app activity." Fortunately, you can disable this tracking by going to this settings page, scrolling down to "Web & App Activity," and turning off all options in this section.

Google's Timeline feature saves your location in Google Maps to create a map of places you've visited. This is useful if you want to keep track of your recent stops; however, Google can use Timeline data to help businesses see how effective their ads were, or how likely you are to visit nearby stores. Its confirmation page confirms this: "Depending on your settings, activity saved as history in your Google Account, including ad interactions, may also be connected to Timeline data to help nearby businesses estimate the likelihood that people will visit their stores. No personal information is shared with businesses.".

It has been revealed that timeline isn't enabled by default, but in case you enabled it a while ago, and are no longer using it, you can turn it off by going to this settings page. Click Turn off, and delete your activity to remove Timeline data from your Google account.

You can't fully escape Google's ads or tracking, but you can disable personalized ads to stop the company from using your account data to show ads. To do this, go to this settings page, and turn off Personalized ads.

Recent findings suggest that while Google claims that it isn't using your emails to train AI, the company does offer AI features that make your emails feel more robotic than human. One of these is "Smart Reply," which offers email reply suggestions such as "Got it. See you soon." I can type that on my own, and I feel uncomfortable with Gmail analyzing the contents of my emails and replies to offer suggestions that I wouldn't use anyway. You can disable this by going to Gmail Settings > General, or by visiting this settings page. Scroll down to "Smart features," and turn off the checkbox next to it. This will disable Smart Compose, Smart Reply, suggestions for pending replies and follow-ups, spelling, grammar, and autocorrect.

According to recent reports, A physical security key is a great security upgrade. It's a physical barrier that prevents most ways to hack into your account remotely. Even if someone discovers your email ID and password, and has access to your two-factor authentication code, they won't get in without physical access to that key. You can check out Google's support page for physical security keys for more information on compatibility and setting up your security keys.

Recent findings suggest that if you're serious about your online privacy and security, I'd advise against keeping your primary credit card saved to your Google account. If your account is compromised or your device is stolen, you risk exposing your credit card to fraud. Instead, use a prepaid virtual card with your Google account. Sites such as Privacy.com offer single-use or merchant-locked prepaid cards, and they allow you to set spending limits too. You can use such services with your Google account to reduce the chances of losing money if your account gets hacked.

Google uses data from Gmail and Google Drive to target ads, which means that your emails, files, and photos could be used for monetization. To stop this, you'll need to disable Personal Intelligence. To turn it off, visit this settings page, and click Turn off Personal Intelligence.

For workflows that require parallel agents, Carbon can act as the coordinator while Hydrogen can power worker and verifier agents to build and test changes simultaneously across isolated workspaces — helping teams ship complex projects faster without driving up token costs.

For developers, Hydrogen costs $1.50 per million input tokens and $7.50 per million output tokens.

Breaking: Robert Pattinson as James Bond Proves That IP Is No Longer the Latest Movie Stars

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Every James Bond casting announcement marks the start of a newly introduced era.
  • It has been revealed that the first Bond of the Amazon MGM era was destined to be even more of a turning point than usual, no matter who landed the role.
  • With Denis Villeneuve at the helm, it arguably marks the first time that Bond has been rebooted by a true auteur director with a distinct preexisting style and fan base.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Every James Bond casting announcement marks the start of a newly introduced era. The fictional MI6 agent has been one of pop culture’s few constants over the past seven decades; and each time a new actor steps into the role, it tells us something about the entertainment landscape we presently inhabit. Bonds can be intensely serious or silly and self-deprecating, and actors have entered the franchise at ages ranging from their late twenties to mid-forties. The role always goes to a member of the Commonwealth, but the variation that’s possible within those parameters has turned the franchise into a vertical wine tasting that illustrates what male movie stardom looks like in each decade. Related Stories Fall Festival Movies Sold: ‘Edward Said: Between Worlds’ About Palestinian-American Author Lands at Kino Lorber The Stop-Motion Tool That’s a Constant in This Crazy, AI-Mixed-Up World.

It has been revealed that the first Bond of the Amazon MGM era was destined to be even more of a turning point than usual, no matter who landed the role. The next film in the franchise will be the first one ever produced without the involvement of the Broccoli family, who have carefully guarded each iteration of the character since “Dr. No” came out in 1962. It marks the biggest movie investment that Amazon has ever made, as the tech giant spent nearly $10 billion to acquire MGM (of which Bond was the clear crown jewel) and then wrestle full control away from the Broccolis.

With Denis Villeneuve at the helm, it arguably marks the first time that Bond has been rebooted by a true auteur director with a distinct preexisting style and fan base. And it follows a Daniel Craig era that many feel took the idea of a dark, realistic James Bond to its logical endpoint with no obvious direction to go next.

When Robert Pattinson was officially revealed as the seventh actor to play 007 on Monday morning, the latest era of the Bond franchise officially took shape. But it also marked the end of a larger Hollywood era in which blue chip legacy characters were seen as infinitely more vital than the people playing them. We spent much of the past decade declaring that intellectual property is the new movie star(s). But casting the current Batman actor as James Bond proves that is no longer the case.

That line of thinking began to take shape in the 2010s, an era of Hollywood that will forever be defined by the phrase “cinematic universe.” As moviegoing became less of a consistent consumer habit and more of an event-driven hobby, the industry found that putting an A-list movie star or two in a new film was no longer enough to guarantee a significant opening weekend. What did work, though, was slapping a Marvel logo in front of something and watching the box office dollars flow in.

Industry observers note that top-tier franchises were places where you went to build your star power, not cash it in. A new Bond or Spider-Man announcement was often the mainstream world’s introduction to a rising star that would be a household name within a few years. The approach was certainly better for the producers who steward these franchises: it ensured that the real value was contained in the stories and iconography that they controlled, making it relatively easy to bring in massive box office hauls with interchangeable actors who often moved onto bigger things before they became too expensive or demanding.

As that formula becomes less workable, it’s fair to wonder where we’ll start going to find our new stars. If you were casting a new Spider-Man in this environment, you probably wouldn’t pick an obscure theater actor like Tom Holland. We’re already seeing more stars come out of independent genre films, one of the few niches that can still be profitable without star power. “Obsession” gave the world its biggest breakout star of 2026 in Inde Navarette, and now she’s heading to the Marvel Cinematic Universe to help lead the “X-Men” franchise. But legacy franchises were once Hollywood’s most reliable path to minting new stars, and the industry will have to get creative if it doesn’t want the pipeline of bankable stars to fizzle out.

In a recent development, from an artistic standpoint, there’s every reason to believe Pattinson will make an excellent Bond. He has already worked with Villeneuve on the upcoming “Dune: Part Three” and has proven himself to be one of his generation’s most versatile leading men. He’s equally capable of playing brooding heroes and sniveling villains; a 2026 slate that includes “The Drama,” “The Odyssey,” and “Primetime” is evidence of both his range and consistent box office appeal. But from a business standpoint, it’s a decision that you wouldn’t make if you didn’t have to.

In a recent development, his deal reportedly costs more money for less commitment than any of the other finalists who screen tested. You’ll be juggling a production and promotion schedule that also includes “The Batman” franchise and other major films. In the run-up to the movie, more eyes will be on the man himself than the timelessness of the brand. And when the time eventually comes to replace him, expectations for the level of actor you need to land will be higher than ever before. It’s the kind of move you make when you simply cannot afford to fail. Nobody would deny that that’s the exact situation Amazon MGM finds itself in, but the mere fact that something as reliable as a newly introduced James Bond movie could place a studio in such a position is notable in and of itself.

It would be reductive to say that the pendulum has entirely swung back towards favoring movie stars. The old model where you could regularly deliver hits by putting George Clooney and Julia Roberts on a poster is certainly nowhere to be found. It might be more accurate to say that we’re in a “more is more” era of Hollywood, where no film is ever guaranteed to become the kind of cultural event that’s required to turn a profit on these massive tentpole budgets. With more competition for audience attention spans than ever before, you need to pair the power of Bond and the power of Pattinson and Villeneuve to feel truly comfortable with your investment.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The following article contains minor spoilers for The Gilded Age season 4, episode 3, "Ain't That Good News".Wedding bells rang for Peggy Scott (Denee Benton) and Dr. William Kirkland (Jordan Donica) in The Gilded Age season 4, and their nuptials included an incredibly poignant tradition. Though the Gilded Age characters enjoyed a fairytale romance all the way to the altar, it wasn't without its complications and tumult, mostly in the form of William's mother, Elizabeth (Phylicia Rashad), who disapproves of everything about Peggy, from her family background to her past as a married woman to her writing career.

In a recent development, however, in The Gilded Age season 4, Elizabeth begrudgingly begins to bring Peggy into the fold since it's clear that her son is determined to marry her. This is more of a forced truce than a genuine change of heart, though. When Elizabeth invites Peggy and her mother, Dorothy (Audra McDonald), into her Newport ladies' club, the Daughters of Friendship, it isn't an olive branch but a shameless attempt to sanitize Peggy's past and make her more palatable to high society as Elizabeth's future daughter-in-law.

Sources indicate that despite Elizabeth maintaining her version of playing nice, The Gilded Age season 4, episode 3 sees her completely upend her efforts. When Peggy's parents present the soon-to-be newlyweds with the broomstick they jumped over when they were married, Elizabeth is horrified, and William tells her that if she can't accept the Scotts, she shouldn't come to the wedding. Ultimately, Peggy persuades her to change her mind, and Elizabeth witnesses the couple jump the broom in the most meaningful scene in The Gilded Age ​​​​​season 4.

Sources indicate that when Peggy's father, Arthur (John Douglas Thompson), and Dorothy were first married, their union wasn't legally recognized because he was enslaved at the time. Though they did eventually have a legal celebration, their initial ceremony involved jumping over the broom they would later gift to Peggy as a symbol of their commitment.

Sources indicate that though there are multiple, conflicting accounts of where the jumping the broom tradition originated, for the African American community, the practice began in the 19th century, at a time when enslaved people did not have the legal right to marry. Accounts of the American tradition's origins differ, with some saying that those who were enslaved chose to jump the broom themselves, while others say that they were forced to do so by their enslavers (via Brides). In Arthur and Dorothy's case, The Gilded Age is adapting the former.

The tradition is widely practiced by North American Black couples today, though it had fallen into disuse at the time Peggy and William were married in the HBO original series. Sonja Warfield, the series' co-showrunner, stated, "We got to take some poetic license, artistic license and keep it because we were trying some other things, but really it needed to be that because that represents the division between the families." (via Deadline) It certainly did, with Elizabeth even willing to miss her only son's wedding over it.

Interestingly, the idea for Peggy and William jumping the broom came from Audra McDonald. Warfield revealed, "We were on set filming Season 3, and Audra McDonald turned to me and she mentioned, ‘When they get married next season, I want them to jump over the broom because Elizabeth will hate that.".

And hate it, she did. Elizabeth's disdain for the practice is entirely rooted in her contempt for the Scott family, specifically Arthur's status as a former enslaved man. As a high-society woman, Elizabeth wants to assimilate, and for her, that means erasing ties and memories of the pre-Emancipation era, and jumping the broom flies in the face of that. However, for Peggy and the Scotts, the tradition is one of reverence, honoring their heritage, which William appreciates, and this is why he gives his mother the ultimatum.

Sources indicate that up until this point, Peggy has shown remarkable patience with Elizabeth, constantly making concessions to keep the peace, though she refuses to compromise on either the broom or her cousin's Fisk Jubilee singers, which Elizabeth also objects to. When Peggy goes to Elizabeth in an attempt to get her to attend the wedding, rather than making a show of putting her foot down, Peggy appeals to Elizabeth's sensibilities as a Christian woman and a mother of good character. She reminds Elizabeth that because she raised William right, he will follow the Bible's guidance, which means that he will always side with his wife.

According to recent reports, peggy keeps her words simple and assertive, and concludes by leaving the decision up to Elizabeth. Happily, Elizabeth not only attends the wedding but holds her tongue as the newlywed couple jumps over the broom. It was a beautiful scene in The Gilded Age, not only symbolic of Peggy's family history but also of her and William leaping into the future together, where they will always choose each other first.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Cyclists who ride with Garmin gear can now appear as live, moving icons on the Waze driving app, and nearby drivers will receive an alert to slow down and watch for them on the road.
  • It has been revealed that for riders already using Garmin devices, opting in costs nothing and adds a upcoming layer of safety, particularly on roads where drivers may not expect cyclists.
  • Recent findings suggest that riders can simply opt in once through Garmin Connect.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Cyclists who ride with Garmin gear can now appear as live, moving icons on the Waze driving app, and nearby drivers will receive an alert to slow down and watch for them on the road.

It has been revealed that for riders already using Garmin devices, opting in costs nothing and adds a upcoming layer of safety, particularly on roads where drivers may not expect cyclists. The feature is rolling out now, but you should be aware of its limitations.

Recent findings suggest that riders can simply opt in once through Garmin Connect. After that, sharing starts automatically when an outdoor cycling activity begins and stops when the ride ends. While a ride is underway, Waze people near the cyclist see a cyclist icon move along the road and receive a Live Cycling Alert reminding them to slow down and stay aware.

Sources indicate that the feature runs on LiveTrack, Garmin's existing live location-sharing tool, which lets friends and family follow a rider's real-time location, speed, course, and more. Garmin says this collaboration extends that peace of mind to motorists, giving them greater awareness of their surroundings.

In a recent development, garmin notes its location sharing is temporary and session-based. The rider's name, identity, and route are hidden, and no personal information is shared or displayed in Waze. Drivers see only an anonymous icon and the alert.

You'll need a few things to get this feature up and running:.

A compatible Garmin Edge bike computer or Garmin watch.

A phone running Garmin Connect with a data connection.

An outdoor cycling activity (the feature doesn't apply to indoor rides).

The good news is using the feature is free: LiveTrack costs nothing on compatible Garmin bike computers and watches, and Waze is free for drivers.

This new feature is a great safety perk, but there are real-world caveats worth considering:.

This feature is for Waze only. Alerts reach drivers only when Waze is open on their phone. Google Maps, which has far more users, is excluded, so a large portion of the drivers you share the road with won't see you this way.

It has been revealed that it depends on your phone's signal. Your position travels from the Garmin to your phone, then to Garmin's servers, then to Waze, and finally to the driver's phone. On a patchy rural signal, a few seconds of lag could put the icon on the wrong side of a bend from where you actually are. A rider who leaves their phone at home or whose phone loses signal simply won't show up on a Waze map, as a ride without a data connection is invisible to Waze.

Finally, remember to treat this safety feature as an extra perk, not a guarantee. At the end of the day, it isn't a replacement for bike lights, bright clothing, and defensive riding.

Sources indicate that hannah covers horror, sci-fi, and games at Collider, where she writes news and features, reviews upcoming releases, and interviews the people who make them. She’s helping build out Collider’s gaming coverage, with Pokémon as one of her specialties. If she isn’t writing about a monster, she’s probably watching one on a tape from her VHS collection.

Macaulay Culkin gets recognized ten times more between November and January, by his own estimate, something he refers to as having “cornered the fourth quarter market.” Kevin McCallister spent Home Alone trying to get everybody to leave him alone, and now the holidays are when people are most likely to stop Culkin in the street.

It has been revealed that culkin sees it at holiday screenings, too. Adults who grew up watching Kevin take on the Wet Bandits are now bringing kids who have no idea what’s about to happen when Harry grabs that doorknob. Culkin has seen that handoff in his own living room, too. In a upcoming interview with Collider's Hannah Hunt, he expressed that the movie has “taken on its own life,” which goes a long way toward explaining why he’s still game to play Kevin 36 years later.

According to recent reports, macaulay Culkin is officially back as Kevin McCallister for McDonald’s new holiday campaign. The limited-time Home Alone Meal starts rolling out internationally on November 24 and hits participating U.S. restaurants on December 1, while supplies last. Each U.S. meal comes with one of four collectible sock designs inspired by the movie, and the menu runs from a Sausage, Egg & Cheese McGriddles at breakfast to a Significant Mac at lunch or dinner.

It has been revealed that little Nero’s may still be the only place Kevin can order a lovely cheese pizza, but McDonald’s is putting that flavor on its fries. The lunch and dinner meals come with Little Nero’s Pizza McShaker Fries, and there’s a Lovely Cheese Pizza Dipping Sauce you can get with McNuggets or McCrispy Strips. The Everything Sundae McFlurry is sold separately and comes with hot fudge, Oreo pieces, and M&M’s. Check out the lineup below. Fans in Los Angeles can also register for the Home Alone Challenge, a pop-up running December 4 and 5 from 5 to 10 p.m. PT. There’s a ball pit, a slingshot challenge, and a free Home Alone Meal for fans who complete the experience.

Culkin’s first thought about bringing Kevin back for McDonald’s was that “it’s about time.” He put the movie and the menu in the same category. You know what the McNuggets are going to taste like, just as you know exactly what’s going to happen when Marv takes his shoes off. You order them and put the movie on anyway. “The actual food and the movie are comfort food, really,” Culkin said. His wife, Brenda Song, was excited about the collaboration, too. “Brenda thinks it’s really cool,” he said. “And that’s really what matters most.”.

It has been revealed that culkin had “no notes” when he saw the meal, and he decided to unbox the collectible socks right there on the call. He gave Grimace his due as “the most famous McDonald’s character of all” before holding up a pair with his own face on them. “If you ever wanted to walk on my face,” he joked, “you can just go to McDonald’s, go get yourself some socks.”.

Industry observers note that as for what Kevin would be like as a grown-up, Culkin figures he’d still get a kick out of “defying authority," which is part of why the movie works so well on kids in the first place. They spend all day being told what they can and can’t do, and here’s somebody their size who gets to tell two grown men exactly where they can step. Culkin thinks the fantasy holds up when you’re old enough to pay for your own pizza, too. “You always have a boss,” he said.

Recent findings suggest that at Culkin’s house, one kid has taken that identification with Kevin a little further. Neither of Culkin’s sons knows their dad played Kevin McCallister, even though they’ve watched Home Alone with him. “They don’t know it’s me,” he told Collider. His oldest, Dakota, has his own explanation. “He thinks he is Kevin.” He looks so much like Culkin did at that age that even a cousin saw the poster while scrolling through a menu and asked why Dakota was in the movie.

In a recent development, the boys ask plenty of other questions while they watch, but Culkin can see Dakota only now starting to put that particular one together. He’s already guessed how the news will break: some kid on the playground, probably named Lenny or Nino, will tell Dakota before he gets the chance. Culkin figures he’ll sit him down afterward and have what he calls a “Beaver Cleaver” moment. Until then, Culkin is happy to let Dakota watch Home Alone and see himself in it, comparing the whole thing to letting his kids believe in Santa Claus:.

“You want to keep that magic as long as possible.".

For now, there’s still time for another Christmas where Dakota gets to be Kevin and his dad gets to sit beside him and watch. The Home Alone Meal comes to McDonald’s in the U.S. on December 1. The movies are available to stream on Disney+.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Robert Pattinson is James Bond. Today (Nov. 16), Amazon MGM Studios confirmed it’s found its new 007 in the form of the British actor most known for his roles as Edward Cullen in “Twilight,” Bruce Wayne in Matt Reeves’ “The Batman” series, and for shouting “somebody get these beggars out of here” in Christopher Nolan’s blockbuster megahit “The Odyssey.”.

In an announcement post on the James Bond website, Pattinson noted, “James Bond is one of the most legendary characters in cinema, and to be entrusted with 007 is the honour of a lifetime.

To say this role is a dream come true is an understatement. I couldn’t be more excited about this partnership and the work ahead with this fantastic team.

Industry observers note that pattinson succeeds Daniel Craig, who bowed out of Bond with 2021’s “No Time to Die,” his fifth outing as the suave superspy. While there is no release date for Pattinson debut as 007, the next installment in the long-running franchise will be directed by Denis Villeneuve, who has already worked with Pattinson on the upcoming “Dune Part 3,” and the next Bond blockbuster will be written by Steven Knight, the creator of “Peaky Blinders.”.

On the casting news, which has been the subject of intense media and fan speculation, Mike Hopkins, Head of Prime Video & Amazon MGM Studios, said, “Today marks a defining moment for our studio and a significant milestone in the history of James Bond as we proudly introduce Robert Pattinson as the next 007.

“This iconic character has captivated audiences around the world for more than six decades, and there’s no doubt that Robert’s remarkable range, magnetic screen presence, and quiet intensity make him an exceptional choice to carry that legacy forward.”.

Industry observers note that pattinson is believed to have won out against a competitive field with several other actors under consideration, including Callum Turner, Jack Lowden, Josh O’Connor and Nicholas Hoult. The rumour mill has frequently flitted through different names, with Pattinson not even on the list the last time we asked our readers who they'd love to be cast as Bond, back in May (opinions were split).

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

Pattinson will be the seventh actor to portray Ian Fleming's beloved character on the big screen in an Eon Productions-produced 007 film. It will be the 26th James Bond movie in the ongoing franchise; the first was 1962's "Dr. No.".

In a recent development, the James Bond casting rumor mill has been in overdrive in recent weeks. And while the odds-on favorite kept switching (first it was Turner, then Lowden), once Pattinson’s name emerged, the wind was only blowing one way.

In many ways, Pattinson was the safe pick. He is the most high-profile star of the names rumored to be in the running, and he has extensive experience working in the Hollywood blockbuster machine, having featured in major franchises like “Twilight,” “Harry Potter” and “The Batman” — the long-delayed sequel to which Pattinson is presently filming.

According to recent reports, however, being the safe pick doesn’t make him the wrong choice, far from it. Pattinson is a guaranteed draw. Earlier this year, alongside Zendaya, he helped drive the off-kilter romantic comedy “The Drama” to $135 million globally, a sign that Pattinson can get butts in seats. His latest movie, “Primetime,” has grossed $62 million worldwide on a sub-$15 million budget.

According to recent reports, more importantly, Pattinson is beloved by a key demographic that Amazon MGM will hope to court with its next Bond movie: younger viewers. The Bond IP goes far with older watchers, but for the franchise to remain at the top of the Hollywood table, it will need to get the TikTok generation watching. Pattinson is the type of actor who can speak to multiple generations.

So, while some longtime 007 fans will bemoan Amazon’s decision to cast an A-lister instead of taking the approach of Bond’s former stewards, the Broccoli family, by selecting a relative unknown. In 2026, Robert Pattinson looks to tick all the right boxes for a new era of Bond.
