Tech Report: The five things to look for when buying a home security camera

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (1963 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Tomsguide

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that home security cameras have become ordinary household hardware.
  • Industry observers note that privacy is a practical buying consideration alongside price, but it still isn’t the thing most buyers put first.
  • In other words, when looking for one of the best home security cameras, it makes more sense to start with the features and subscription, rather than the headline numbers on the spec sheet.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that home security cameras have become ordinary household hardware. SafeHome.org’s 2026 survey of 2,435 US adults found that 61% of households have at least one, up from 52% in 2024 and 42% in 2023, while video doorbells have reached 48% of households. Renters drove much of that growth. Their adoption rate jumped from 42% to 54% between 2024 and 2026, which makes sense given how many battery-powered cameras can be mounted without drilling and moved at the end of a lease.

Industry observers note that privacy is a practical buying consideration alongside price, but it still isn’t the thing most buyers put first. SafeHome ranks ease of use at 50% and monthly cost at 46%, ahead of self-installation, brand reputation and upfront price.

In other words, when looking for one of the best home security cameras, it makes more sense to start with the features and subscription, rather than the headline numbers on the spec sheet. That, of course, can make finding the right one even harder. Here are some things to keep in mind when looking for a home security camera.

Arlo's Essential Wireless Security Camera helps you keep an eye on all the places that matter most. With Smart Detection for people, pets and packages, along with real-time alerts and color night vision, this high-quality security camera will give you peace of mind. Get two wire-free, rechargeable cameras this Black Friday, and with easy installation, they'll be up and running for the holidays.

The best way to figure out what security camera is right for you is to start with thinking about what you actually need a camera for.

It has been revealed that A video doorbell suits packages and callers because its head-to-toe view and two-way talk are built around a front door. A driveway or yard needs a weatherproof outdoor camera, while a floodlight camera covers a broader area and adds deterrence. As a rule, cover each entry point instead of asking one camera to watch the entire property.

Prices generally fall into three useful bands. Budget models can be found for as little as $29, but you can still find features like 2K video and a pan-and-tilt designs that physically turn to cover a room. Mid-range models (around $100) offer good value, with additional features or better designs. Premium hardware reaches the $249 level and beyond, where you'll find such things as 4K video.

The number of megapixels figure on the box matters less than how many pixels land on a face. A 4-megapixel camera with a 2,560-pixel-wide image and an 80-degree lens can, under the older IEC 62676-4 identification guideline, identify someone at roughly 20 feet. A 4K camera captures 3,840 pixels across, but pair it with a wider 100-degree lens and that estimate rises only to about 21 feet. The extra pixels have been spent on width, so with the same lens, 4K gives you roughly twice the identification distance of 1080p, not four times.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

According to recent reports, treat these numbers as geometry rather than guarantees, especially since the IEC standard for measuring detail at distance was revised in 2025. It uses 500 pixels per meter of scene width for validating a known person and 1,500 for high-certainty identification, while many spec sheets still rely on the older 250-pixel guideline. For a doorbell, 1080p is generally enough because visitors are close. For outdoor cameras, 2K, usually around 2,560 pixels across, is the sensible default. Pay for 4K when you need more detail at distance rather than simply a wider view, and check that your storage and Wi-Fi can handle it.

That stated, two ordinary cameras in the right places will often beat one expensive 4K model covering everything badly.

“Spend less time chasing the highest resolution number in isolation. More detail can be useful, but placement, nighttime visibility, and useful notifications deserve just as much attention,” indicates Lars Felber, director of PR at Eve Systems. “A camera pointed at the wrong part of the porch can miss what matters regardless of its resolution.”.

Judge a camera on its night footage, too. Infrared night vision uses light outside the visible spectrum to produce a black-and-white image in darkness, so it can show details relatively cleanly, but not with any color. Color night vision needs ambient light from a streetlamp or porch, or a built-in light — though often color night vision is a little less detailed, and usually can't see as far.

In a recent development, watch for smeared movement too, since some battery cameras reduce their frame rate at night. Keep the lens away from glass and nearby eaves, which can bounce infrared light back into it.

Industry observers note that power decides where a camera can go and whether it can record continuously. Battery models are the easiest to install and the most renter-friendly, but they sleep until motion wakes them, so you get event clips rather than a full timeline and may lose the moments just before a trigger. Plug-in models remove charging breaks but leave you with a cable to route. Hardwired doorbells and floodlights can support 24/7 recording.

Recent findings suggest that power over Ethernet, usually shortened to PoE, carries power and data down one network cable for a more dependable connection. PoE requires cabling and a compatible switch or recorder, which is more work than most people want for a single doorbell. Solar models are the compromise. Solar models still have a battery, but solar panels keep the battery topped up so you don't need to worry about manual charging.

According to recent reports, A solar panel is often the more practical upgrade for an awkward outdoor mount. Just about every manufacturer that makes one of the best outdoor security cameras offers a compatible panel. You’ll need a position with dependable sun, and short winter days can still leave the camera reliant on its battery, though it still beats climbing a ladder every few weeks.

It has been revealed that outdoor hardware also needs a weather rating. IP65, which means dust-tight and protected against low-pressure water jets, is a common floor for outdoor cameras and suits eave-mounted units, while IP66 is the better target for fully exposed walls. Check the stated operating temperature too. Arlo rates the Pro 6 down to −4°F, while cheaper models don’t always cope as well with freezing conditions. If you live somewhere that gets truly cold, like Canada, many models may not work for you.

Before drilling, test Wi-Fi at the exact mount point with your phone. Exterior walls and foil-backed insulation can badly weaken 5GHz Wi-Fi, which is fast but relatively short-ranged. Many budget cameras use only 2.4GHz, which reaches farther but contends with more household congestion.

Finally, check your upload speed if you blueprint to run several cloud cameras. Local recording to a memory card or hub doesn’t use that upload link, but continuous cloud video can saturate it surprisingly quickly.

It has been revealed that often, the price you pay for the camera itself is just a starting point. You still have to store video — and unless you can do so locally, you may have to pay for a subscription.

Some cameras have microSD card slots built into them. A microSD memory card is cheap, works without internet and can support continuous recording, but a thief can take it along with the camera. Cloud storage preserves an off-site copy and makes playback easy from anywhere, though it usually means a subscription fee, plus you may or may not be interested in cloud storage for privacy reasons.

A local hub splits the difference. These live in your house, but are connected to your cameras wirelessly, so footage can survive both a damaged camera and an internet outage. A hybrid setup is generally the better choice, with local recording for continuity and cloud copies for important events.

According to recent reports, “One of the most crucial things to look for in a home security camera is if a subscription is required to set up and use the device,” says Carney. “Going into the purchasing process, consumers should be aware that some security companies tack on a required subscription as a hidden cost without being transparent about it at purchase.”.

In a recent development, without a blueprint, some organization's cameras will only let you view live events, and not save recordings, or access all of a camera's features. Be sure to look at the price of the subscription, and see if what's being offered is worth the long-term investment.

Once footage is being recorded, the next problem is getting alerted only when it matters. A camera that pings every time a car passes will eventually be ignored. Custom motion zones, sensible sensitivity controls and reliable person, vehicle and package detection do more for daily use than another AI label. At a door, two-way audio is worth having too, so you can speak to a courier without opening it.

According to recent reports, “A camera can be very advanced and still fail at its only job if notifications are delayed,” claims Rod Sides, founder of Loxx Boxx. “Worse, if it displays too many notifications in a way that you haven’t customized, you’re more likely to overlook the one key notification that may pop up.”.

According to recent reports, privacy policies deserve as much attention as the video specs. End-to-end encryption means only your devices hold the keys, so the camera organization can’t decrypt the footage. Apple’s HomeKit Secure Video works this way by default. Google encrypts Nest footage in transit and at rest, but not end-to-end.

In a recent development, “Privacy should be part of the buying decision from the beginning. Ask where footage is analyzed and stored, who can access it and whether both live video and recordings have end-to-end encryption,” notes Felber. “Simply working with Apple Home doesn’t automatically mean a camera supports HomeKit Secure Video, so check for that feature explicitly.”.

Recent findings suggest that and don’t forget the microphone, since many cameras record audio by default. Recording a private conversation without everyone’s consent can break the law in all-party consent states such as California. If you don’t need sound or two-way talk, switching it off is the safer default.

What’s actually worth paying for? Reliable person and package detection with activity zones, a mechanical privacy shutter on an indoor camera, local storage that keeps recording through an internet outage, and night performance verified in real footage. Solar power or PoE is worth the premium if the alternative is repeated ladder trips, and a subscription only makes sense if you can afford it for five years. You probably don't need 4K on most standard setups, either.

“What consumers can spend less time worrying about is having the highest resolution or every bell and whistle on the market,” says Zavin. “Instead, focus on what the camera can actually do when a potential threat arises.”.

According to recent reports, for most homes, a well-placed 2K camera with accurate detection and a local fallback is the better buy. Step up to 4K or paid AI search if you have a specific use for them, not just because they're available.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When shooting both photos and videos on my iPhone, I make regular use of a few different third-party apps, mostly because I like to take manual control.

But a combination of the fresh Pro controls on the iPhone 18 Pro and a new feature introduced with iOS 27 means there are more times when I can stick to Apple’s stock Camera app. If you aren’t already using customizable controls, I highly recommend doing so ….

Recent findings suggest that developers know that a major reason for using third-party camera apps is being able to use them in much the same way you would a standalone camera. A key part of this is having easy access to manual control over things like aperture (on the iPhone 18 Pro), shutter speed, white balance, and choosing between manual and auto focus. Those settings are right there on the main screen of almost all third-party apps.

With the iPhone 18 Pro, the same set of controls are also available in Apple’s stock camera app. By default, these are tucked inside a menu, requiring an initial tap to open it. As we noted back in September, however, iOS 27 brings customizable controls to the camera app.

In a recent development, simply open the menu and tap the Edit button (top-left when holding the phone vertically) and you can add any of the controls to the main screen. This makes them available in a single tap.

For still photography, I have these:.

It has been revealed that aperture, shutter speed, and white balance as these are the three main manual controls I use. Exposure compensation, because sometimes the only reason I want to take manual control is to increase or decrease the exposure, and that provides a faster way of doing so (quicker than the alternative drag up/down within the photo, in my experience). Finally, I have one-tap access to the histogram to help in setting exposure.

Sources indicate that it’s a similar story in video mode. I again have aperture and white balance along with exposure compensation and the histogram. But here I add instant access to frame-rate and focus modes (as I’m more likely to switch focus mode when shooting video).

Of course, third-party apps still have an key role, but this one change has made a massive difference to me when using the stock camera app for both photos and video.

Recent findings suggest that do you make use of this feature yourself? If so, please share the details in the comments.

The AX1500 offers up to 1.5Gbps, the AX3000 doubles that and adds a 2.5Gbps WAN port, while the Wi-Fi 7-enabled Roam 7 reaches up to 3.6Gbps.

Sources indicate that the TP-Link Archer AX21 V5 AX1800 is down to $54.99 from $89.99, saving you $35 on an affordable Wi-Fi 6 router for everyday home use. Its dual-band connection offers combined theoretical speeds of up to 1.8Gbps, which should be sufficient for typical activities like streaming, video calls, and browsing across several devices.

Sources indicate that for homes with faster internet intends, multiple gamers, or lots of connected devices, TP-Link's Archer BE700 and BE770 offer tri-band Wi-Fi 7, including access to the 6GHz band for compatible devices. As for pricing, the TP-Link Archer BE700 is down to $248 from $349.99, saving you just over $100. It offers theoretical speeds of up to 15Gbps, a 2.5Gbps LAN port, and three Gigabit LAN ports. For just $52 more, the Archer BE770 (now $299.99, was $369.99) bumps speeds up to 18Gbps and adds a dedicated 10Gbps LAN port, making it better suited to high-speed network storage and large file transfers.

The TP-Link Deco BE25 is down to $99.98 from $129.99, saving you $30 on a Wi-Fi 7 router designed to work as part of a mesh network. It offers dual-band wireless speeds of up to 5Gbps, two 2.5Gbps Ethernet ports, and AI-driven roaming that helps connected devices switch between Deco units as you move around your home.

Priscilla Presley scored a partial victory in her bitter $50 million legal war with her former business advisers Monday, persuading a judge to dismiss four of the 21 claims filed against her in a fraud and breach of contract lawsuit.

But Presley failed to persuade the judge to spike lengthy paragraphs from the lawsuit concerning her divorce from Elvis Presley and the shocking 2023 death of their daughter, Lisa Marie Presley. The judge blasted some of the “extremely long” complaint as “gratuitous and mean-spirited” but remarked striking the disputed language would make little difference because the claims were already public.

Sources indicate that the new ruling issued Monday dismissed claims that Presley interfered with a cosmetics contract and improperly used her own name, image, and likeness in violation of an alleged agreement with business advisers Brigitte Kruse and Kevin Fialko. Ruling from the bench, Los Angeles County Judge Mark Epstein stated the allegations were not sufficiently supported by facts in the complaint. Though she won on four causes of action, Presley lost her bid to toss out 10 other claims related to fraud, breach of contract, and the alleged misappropriation of funds allegedly belonging to companies set up with Kruse and Fialko.

Among the allegations Presley sought to remove from the lawsuit were claims that her “thirst for power and money was insatiable” during her divorce from Elvis Presley and that she prematurely “pulled the plug” on their daughter, Lisa Marie Presley, for financial gain. Lisa Marie died in 2023 after being hospitalized with a small bowel obstruction linked to a prior bariatric surgery. (In her memoir, Softly, As I Leave You: Life After Elvis, Presley wrote that Lisa Marie went into cardiac arrest at the hospital and was resuscitated, but then doctors told her she had “little brain activity” and would have “no quality of life” if kept on life support.).

In a recent development, monday’s hearing came three years after Presley’s legal battle with Kruse and Fialko first reached the courts. Kruse, a prominent memorabilia dealer, filed the initial legal action in Florida in October 2023, accusing Presley of abandoning the series of companies they formed to capitalize on her name, image, and likeness. It has been revealed that presley filed a separate lawsuit in Los Angeles in July 2024, accusing Kruse and Fialko of elder abuse. She described Kruse as a “con artist and pathological liar” who had misappropriated more than $1 million and fraudulently induced her to sign agreements giving the pair an 80 percent stake in some of her business ventures. Kruse and Fialko subsequently moved their claims from Florida to California, filing a $50 million cross-complaint last year.

In a recent development, in video exclusively obtained by Rolling Stone, Presley is seen signing the contracts behind her deals with Kruse and Fialko. In the ensuing legal battle, Kruse has claimed Presley was facing “impending financial ruin” when Kruse and Fialko stepped in to help rescue the cultural icon. Kruse alleges Presley then cut her out because her financial circumstances changed dramtaically in the wake of Lisa Marie Presley’s death. As Rolling Stone previously reported, two weeks after Lisa Marie died on Jan. 12, 2023, Presley challenged a 2016 amendment to her daughter’s trust that removed her as a co-trustee. Presley later reached a settlement with granddaughter Riley Keough that granted her a $1 million lump-sum payment, a $100,000 annual salary, and burial rights near Elvis at Graceland.

On Monday, Judge Epstein gave Kruse and Fialko an opportunity to amend their complaint and revive some of the dismissed claims under different legal theories, potentially including breach of contract. But he cautioned against expanding on the background paragraphs Presley challenged as “inflammatory.”.

Recent findings suggest that “If you want to cut out some of the stuff written for a different audience, I wouldn’t shed any tears,” Epstein said. Authentic Brands acquired certain commercial rights to the Presley name in 2013 through its purchase of Elvis Presley’s licensing business. #16326. Latest Update: I’ve never seen a James Bond movie, but I will now that Robert Pattinson is the new 007

Latest Update: I’ve never seen a James Bond movie, but I will now that Robert Pattinson is the new 007

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (891 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Tomsguide

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • I have this running bit where I call Robert Pattinson my girlfriend.
  • I've never seen a James Bond movie all the way through, a fact that shocked my (mostly male) coworkers this morning.
  • Recent findings suggest that no, my excitement for Pattinson's 007 reign doesn't stem from nostalgia, but from a quiet fascination that's sparked into an obsession over the past decade.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I have this running bit where I call Robert Pattinson my girlfriend. It started sometime after "The Lighthouse" because old men gone bitter with yearning is very much my brand of terminally ill brain worm, and the joke's only gotten funnier with the stellar year the "Twilight" star's had. Yesterday, Amazon MGM Studios announced that Pattinson is taking up the mantle of 007, and I broke the news to the group chat with the following message: "my girlfriend is gonna be James Bond!" No explanation needed.

I've never seen a James Bond movie all the way through, a fact that shocked my (mostly male) coworkers this morning. Now that my favorite weird little guy is in the lead, I'm willing to break that streak. Before you go calling me a rabid fangirl, I have another confession: I first watched "Twilight" all the way through this year. I attempted once in high school but had to bail at the baseball scene where the level of unabashed white corniness on display had my eyes nearly rolling out of my skull.

Recent findings suggest that no, my excitement for Pattinson's 007 reign doesn't stem from nostalgia, but from a quiet fascination that's sparked into an obsession over the past decade. This, the man who insists he's "spiritually Gen Z" despite pushing 40, who lies in interviews for fun, who dragged millions of screaming fans into theaters by being a brooding, sexy vampire for a series he openly despises. And I suspect his casting has activated those same millennial women like sleeper agents who will no doubt propel this latest Bond run into one of the most commercially successful to date. With many, like myself, turning out for their first Bond venture in theaters ever.

Industry observers note that action films are a notable blind spot in my cinema knowledge, one that I've been trying to fill in recent years since writing about streaming for Tom's Guide. It's not that I avoided them, per say, just that they didn't immediately appeal to me in the same way as my favorite genres — horror, art house, and damn near anything animated — did.

All the Jason Bournes, John Wicks, and Ethan Hunts of the world struck me as carbon copies of one another made in a lab to be propelled through one bombastic shoot out after the next. Now that I've caught up on a few of these iconic franchises, that opinion still rings true, though I've gained an appreciation for the kind of high-octane set pieces action fans still talk about to this day.

Recent findings suggest that with Pattinson at the helm of the next Bond film, for the first time in my life, I'm excited to see a 007 movie in theaters. His talent and magnetism, even as some of the most pathetic characters I've ever seen on screen, is something straight out of the golden age of Hollywood.

Today's Bond announcement is the cherry on top of a year that's cemented Pattinson as a once in a generation acting talent. Between making our skin crawl as the charismatically slimy Chris Hansen in "Primetime" to going viral for shouting “somebody get these beggars out of here” in Christopher Nolan’s blockbuster megahit “The Odyssey" and proving once again that no one does pathetic quite as well as he does in "The Drama," it's been a banner year for Pattison.

According to recent reports, the British actor most known for his roles as Edward Cullen in “Twilight,” Cedric Diggory in "Harry Potter," and Bruce Wayne in Matt Reeves’ “The Batman” series will now succeed Daniel Craig as everyone's favorite suave superspy. There's no release date yet for Pattinson's debut as 007, though we do know Denis Villeneuve, who has already worked with Pattinson on the upcoming “Dune Part 3,” will be at the helm with a script by "Peaky Blinders" creator Steven Knight.

It's clear Amazon MGM is trying to appeal to younger viewers with this pick too. After being around for over 70 years, James Bond's built a reputation as your father's (or maybe even grandfather's) favorite spy franchise. As Bruce Wayne in "The Batman," Pattinson proved he can bring a fresh edge to an iconic character without losing the mass appeal that makes a franchise work. With "The Batman" sequel currently in production, he’s also firmly established as a leading man audiences will turn out to see. For a franchise looking to usher in its next era, that's a pretty convincing résumé.

By the way if you have seen some Bond movies, why not try playing our multiple choice Bond quiz, below?

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Under the glow of stage lights on the second day of the 83rd National Folk Festival, Mavis Staples, whose stature and seniority make her the de facto headliner of the three-day music and culture gathering, is finally addressing her jubilant audience.

“Mississippi, Lord!” she shouts to a roar of approval from a crowd of 2,000 spectators in Jackson, Mississippi, that has spilled over from the seats to a standing-room-only stage front.

Three days after voters here selected Scott Colom as the state’s first Black U.S. Senator since Reconstruction, the crowd seems to anticipate what she’s going to say next. It’s a sentiment that has been on the lips of festivalgoers throughout the weekend.

“I have always been proud to say I’m from Mississippi, but now I’m more proud than ever!” Staples continues, her rousing banter sounding more like a Sunday-morning sermon than the stage vamps of a soul superstar. “I didn’t think I was gonna cry no more after Obama, but I’m telling you, I remarked, ‘Let me get my bucket!’”.

Recent findings suggest that staples, 87, has a history and pedigree that connects Mississippi’s current historic moment back to the Civil Rights Movement, and indeed to the roots of American music. (On Monday morning, she received three 2027 Grammy nominations on the strength of her latest album, Sad and Beautiful World.).

As the frontwoman of the Staple Singers, the family band started by her father, Roebuck “Pops” Staples, her husky contralto is synonymous with resistance songs like “Freedom Highway” and funk-soul hits like “I’ll Take You There.” Her musical lineage traces all the way to Dockery Farm, the Delta sharecropping plantation where Pops lived and worked alongside blues originators Robert Johnson, Howlin’ Wolf, and Son House.

At her final scheduled performance of 2026, Staples, fronting a five-piece band, performed an hour-plus set stacked with songs reflecting the symbolism of Colom’s win. Early in the show, the audience applauded declarations like “No political domination!” from the 1973 song “If You’re Ready (Come Go With Me).” Another round of cheers arrived after she delivered the line “Take the sheet off your face, boy, it’s a brand-latest day” from 1971’s “Respect Yourself.” Editor’s picks The 250 Greatest Albums of the 21st Century So Far The 100 Best TV Episodes of All Time The 500 Greatest Albums of All Time 100 Best Movies of the 21st Century.

In a recent development, “I think every message within her songs is just uplifting,” says Gabrielle Jackson, 19, after the performance. A college student who grew up in Cleveland, Mississippi, barely five miles east of Dockery, Jackson often heard the Staple Singers’ songs at home. “Being a music major and somebody who just loves music, seeing things like this is very inspiring.”.

In a recent development, stages across downtown Jackson hosted artists from Mississippi as well as other regions, expressing the cultural diversity found across the nation. The National Council for the Traditional Arts produces the annual event in partnership with local organizers.

Hill Country blues singer Cedric Burnside, a grandson of the late R.L. Burnside from the Holly Springs area who learned how to keep a juke jumping by playing drums behind his “Big Daddy” R.L. as a child, performed with his band and in collaboration with another North Mississippi standout, the Rising Star Fife and Drum Band. Led by fife player Shardé Thomas, Rising Star perform in the West African-meets-rural-blues tradition popularized in the region by her grandfather, Otha Turner.

“This festival gives you a chance to be who you are,” Burnside notes while tuning his guitar before taking the stage. “I come from a background where my Big Daddy, R.L. Burnside, he was a sharecropper, and he played Hill Country blues stripped down. Some people would look at the rawness as being like, ‘That’s not really great music, because it don’t have this, and it don’t have that.’ It’s the rawness what makes it so special.” Related Content Mississippi Is Sending a Democrat to the Senate Wildfire Smoke Forces the Black Keys, Creed, and More to Postpone Concerts Nolan Wells’ Parents Announce Public Funeral Arrangements: ‘We Want to Celebrate’ Him What We Know About Nolan Xavier Wells, the Teen Found Dead in Mississippi.

Industry observers note that the lineup also featured Mississippi soul-blues musicians Eddie Cotton Jr. and Dexter Allen, as well as dobro master Jerry Douglas and the Savoy Family Cajun Band. Jackson-based hip-hop producer Hollywood Luck mixed a set that included “Cadillac on 22s,” a 2003 hit from another local, David Banner.Acts like Rebolú, Rahim AlHaj Trio, and Capoeira Luanda expressed a broader musical diaspora through Colombian dance, Iraqi oud, and Brazilian capoeira, respectively.

Meanwhile, gospel quartet Annie and the Caldwells — a family group out of West Point, Mississippi, signed to David Byrne’s Luaka Bop label — put on a trio of high-energy, improvisational gospel performances that reverberated throughout the downtown streets.

“They had strong voices that carried — you could hear them all throughout the whole festival,” says 32-year-old Kristina Oxendine from Clinton, Mississippi. Oxendine caught the group’s Friday night performance with his sister, Katrina, 29, and the pair decided to come back to see them again. “They put a twist on songs that we already knew and remixed it themselves and made it their own,” Katrina says, citing the 1990 cut “Feels Good” by Tony! Toni! Toné!.

Annie Caldwell, 69, started singing when she was 10, and in the mid-1970s performed with siblings as the Staples Jr. in tribute to her favorite group. Annie and the Caldwells carry on the family tradition but with a different name and faces. Daughter Deborah Caldwell Moore, wearing chunky black spectacles and a mane of bright silver curls, is likely responsible for the pipes that brought the Oxendines to the stage — she takes the lead throughout most of the gig, sing-shouting her lines with an intensity that recalls James Brown, David Lee Roth, and, of course, Mavis Staples.

Festivalgoers had opportunities to experience Mississippi culture in other ways, too. Cooking demonstrations showed the century-long influence of Chinese culture in the Delta, while Geno Lee of the Big Apple Inn on Jackson’s Farish Street, a historic Black thoroughfare, served up famed local bites like pig-ear sliders. While she was introducing her band onstage, Staples took a moment to applaud bassist Greg Boaz for having the courage to try one.

It has been revealed that by 8 p.m., all the attention was on the main stage and Staples. As the crowd grew, Reena Evers-Everette — who was 8 years old when she heard the gunfire that killed her father, Civil Rights hero Medgar Evers, in their Jackson driveway — was vibrant backstage, reminiscing on seeing Staples as a child in Mound Bayou, where they both spent time as kids. Her uncle, Charles Evers, also produced a series of annual Medgar Evers Homecoming concerts, which the Staple Singers played several times.

In a recent development, “This [festival] just brings back the good feelings, and the understanding of what is really important —and that’s togetherness,” she notes. “When Mavis belts it out, you just melt. It’s a unifying sound, and it’s a sound that’s really unique to the South.”.

According to recent reports, like others in attendance, she’s also aglow at the results of the recent election that will send Colom to the Senate. “All of Mississippi demonstrated out,” she claims. “It indicates that there’s time for a change. Sam Cooke is not here, but he could go ahead and see that change is gonna come, because it is, in the best way.” Trending Stories Watch Buffalo Springfield Come Together for the First Time in Many Years Jennifer Lopez Teases New Music on ‘Fallon’: ‘This Does Feel Like a Happy Era’ Cynthia Erivo, Travis Barker Honor Phil Collins With Massive Vocals, Big Drums at Rock Hall Ceremony Miley Cyrus Shares Sweet Memory of Godmother Dolly Parton as They Earn a Grammy Nod Together.

Balancing the hope in her voice is the specter of the Old Capitol building rising just behind the stage where Staples will perform. Built in 1839, the Greek Revival structure bore witness to many of the wrongs Evers-Everette and others believe are one step closer to being righted. On its floor, legislators drafted Mississippi’s articles of secession in 1861. Then, in 1890, they drafted and signed a newly introduced state constitution that enshrined Jim Crow laws consigning its Black citizens to second-class status for the better part of a century.

In a recent development, “At first, I stated I’m on cloud nine,” Evers-Everette states of Colom’s victory. “Then I said, no, I’m on cloud 2026, and I’m staying there until 2027. And then 2028. And I’m gonna rise higher and higher, because this nation and this world is getting ready to soar.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

iOS 27.3 is coming next month, and during the beta so far there are three latest features I’ve been using almost every day.

Siri AI in iOS 27 brings major upgrades by providing world knowledge, personal context features, and being more conversational than ever. But one previously announced Siri improvement—an expanded set of actions for Apple apps—didn’t make the cut in iOS 27.0.

Now in iOS 27.3, though, Apple is rolling out its first set of new app actions for Siri AI.

Siri AI has latest capabilities across apps like Calendar, Files, Journal, Mail, Maps, Messages, Music, Notes, Photos, Preview, Reminders, Safari, Shortcuts, and Weather. It’s a substantial step toward making voice-driven computing more powerful on Apple platforms, and I’ve had fun experimenting with everything new Siri can do.

Read more: iOS 27.3 expands Siri AI with many new capabilities across Apple apps.

According to recent reports, apple Health gets a big overhaul in iOS 27.3, with a fresh design and upcoming features that utilize Apple Intelligence for more personalized health insights. Per Apple:.

Recent findings suggest that the updated experience includes a latest Insights tab that surfaces timely, holistic summaries spanning heart, sleep, readiness, fitness, vitals, and cycle tracking data throughout the day. A dedicated For You section delivers intelligent recommendations tailored to a user’s daily habits — such as practical guidance to adjust a wind-down routine following consecutive nights of interrupted sleep. The app pairs data with dynamic health content, offering educational videos and articles featuring Health app clinical experts.

It has been revealed that in my testing so far, I’ve especially enjoyed getting up-to-date guidance every day on my health metrics, browsing the deep collection of newly introduced educational videos and articles, and understanding all the factors that contribute to longevity. I think Apple is moving the right direction with this enhancement.

Read more: iOS 27.3 adds all-latest Apple Health app, details here.

If you have an Apple Watch Series 12 or Apple Watch Ultra 4, iOS 27.3 adds a powerful latest feature called Siri Recap that “ambiently takes notes on your conversations throughout your day and creates high-level Apple Intelligence–generated summaries that you can use later to jog your memory.”.

Sources indicate that "iOS 27.3 adds three newly introduced features I've used almost every day", "Apple Maps in iOS 27 has hidden new feature I’ve been loving". What's with these terrible clickbait titles lately? Did we go back to 2014?

Industry observers note that siri Recap functions like an outsourced short-term memory reserve. The data it collects is saved inside the Siri app in a new Recaps tab, where it lives for seven days and is then deleted—unless you manually save a specific recap.

So far in the beta, I’ve found the summaries Siri generates to strike a good balance of being helpful but not too invasive. It reminds me of key details, but there’s nothing I’ve seen that feels overly sensitive or personalized. That may change over time the more I use it, but so far I think this could prove a really valuable feature.

Read more: watchOS 27.3 adds upcoming Apple Watch feature that I absolutely love.

Which newly introduced iOS 27.3 features have you been enjoying in the beta? Let us know in the comments.

In a recent development, upgrading your TV's sound doesn't necessarily mean spending a fortune on a full home theater setup, especially with early Black Friday deals bringing substantial discounts on soundbars and audio systems from Sony, Bose, Samsung, and LG. Sony has some of the biggest price cuts, with savings of up to 32% across select Bravia Theater models, including more than $700 off its premium Theater Trio system.

Samsung's Dolby Atmos soundbars are also discounted by as much as $400, while Bose and LG have more affordable options for anyone looking to improve dialogue clarity, add some bass, or enjoy surround sound without a complicated setup. Whether you're shopping for a compact speaker for a bedroom TV or a more immersive system for movie nights, here are the deals worth considering.

For anyone building a premium home theater around a large TV, the Sony Bravia Theater Trio is down to $1,498 from $2,199.99, saving you $701.99, or roughly 32%. Unlike a conventional soundbar, the Trio uses three separate front speakers for the left, center, and right channels, helping spread dialogue and effects across a wider soundstage. You can read PCMag’s “excellent” review for more details.

According to recent reports, the Sony Bravia Theater Bar 7 is down to $718 from $869 for anyone who wants a single soundbar under the TV. Its nine speakers include upward- and side-firing drivers that widen the soundstage and give Dolby Atmos some height, but there’s no subwoofer, so the now $898 Bar 7 with a wireless sub bundle (down from $1,099.99) might be the better pick for deeper bass.

How to safeguard your property during the darker winter months

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1859 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Tomsguide

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that as we head into the winter (at least in the Northern hemisphere), it's getting darker, earlier.
  • In a recent development, but the risk is actually more complicated than the old image of a burglar creeping around at midnight, and so is the defense.
  • According to recent reports, the darker months have arrived, and Arlo's Essential Outdoor Pan Tilt Zoom Security Camera's 360-degree pan and 180-degree tilt capabilities keep an eye on every corner of your property with an integrated spotlight and color night vision.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that as we head into the winter (at least in the Northern hemisphere), it's getting darker, earlier. That means that by the time you get home from work, it might already be dark. Some police departments have noticed the same shift and are already planning around it. For example, as daylight saving time ended, the Palos Verdes Estates Police Department in California warned residents that an early sunset gives burglars more chances to spot homes that look unoccupied, and urged people to leave a few interior lights on or use timers, and to keep entryways lit. It's a useful starting point, and a fairly simple one.

In a recent development, but the risk is actually more complicated than the old image of a burglar creeping around at midnight, and so is the defense. Good locks, lighting and habits do a lot of the work, and many of those checks cost almost nothing. A camera or alarm then adds a layer on top, since it indicates you what's happening and lets you act on it.

According to recent reports, the darker months have arrived, and Arlo's Essential Outdoor Pan Tilt Zoom Security Camera's 360-degree pan and 180-degree tilt capabilities keep an eye on every corner of your property with an integrated spotlight and color night vision. Automatic motion tracking follows activity so you can stay aware of what's happening, and Smart Detection for people, vehicles, pets and packages helps you distinguish between a cat passing through your backyard and a potential security threat.

Thankfully, burglaries are on the decline. The FBI's 2024 burglary rate of 229.2 per 100,000 people was about 69% below the 2005 rate, and the FBI's 2025 data show burglary falling roughly another 16% in 2025.

But falling crime doesn't make prevention optional, because the FBI's 2024 data show that just 15.9% of property crimes were cleared by arrest or exceptional means, and burglary has run a bit lower, at 14.1% in 2019. Getting property back is, realistically, a much weaker initiative than keeping someone out.

According to recent reports, package theft is harder to pin down. In Security.org's 2026 survey, 30% of American adults said they'd had a package stolen at some point, up from 24% a year earlier, though the survey wasn't weighted and the increase alone doesn't prove the rate has risen. It does put the exposed parts of a property, including porches, driveways, yards and garages, at the center of a winter plan, since long nights make an approach much easier.

Industry observers note that winter doesn't turn burglars into night owls, but it does change when your home is most exposed. In the Bureau of Justice Statistics' analysis of household burglary, which covers 2003 to 2007, 43% of burglaries of empty homes happened between 6 a.m. and 6 p.m., compared with 26% overnight. In winter, though, sunset moves into the commute window, so a house that's empty and unlit at 5:30 p.m. can look as unoccupied as one at midnight. And the evening stakes are higher, since someone was home in 61% of nighttime burglaries versus 33% of daytime ones.

Sources indicate that A sizable share of break-ins also don't need force. The FBI's 2019 breakdown classed 37.8% of burglaries as unlawful entry with no force used. In the dark, an unlocked back door or ground-floor window is easier to try without anyone noticing, which is why the winter checklist starts with locks.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

Lock everything, even when you're home, and that includes first-floor windows and any upstairs window reachable from a flat roof or ladder.

Industry observers note that on main doors, a deadbolt offers far more resistance than a simple spring latch. Fit it with long screws that anchor the strike plate, the metal plate around the lock bolt, into the frame rather than just the decorative trim. Look for a deadbolt certified to the ANSI/BHMA A156.40 residential standard, ideally with an A grade for security. One of the best smart locks can help too — most offer an auto-lock setting (make sure it's switched on), so even if you forget to lock the door, it won't remain unlocked.

Windows need more than a handle pulled shut. Fit a working lock to every accessible window, and add stops that limit how far it can open. A wooden or metal bar in a patio door's track stops it from sliding, even when the latch is easily broken.

A peephole or door chain gives you a way to check a caller before opening up. Check ID from anyone claiming to be from a utility company, and be especially skeptical of urgent repair offers after bad weather. The FTC warns that scammers often turn up after severe weather, pushing homeowners to sign a contract right away or pay up front, and advises confirming a contractor's license and insurance before agreeing to anything.

It has been revealed that outside, lock the side gate, shed and garage, since long winter nights make outbuildings an easier target. Put ladders and tools away, since they can also help someone reach or force the house. Frost or obscure garage windows too, so nobody can casually browse your belongings from the street.

Industry observers note that the boundary of the property matters too. Low front hedges preserve visibility, while gravel makes a quiet approach considerably harder. Anti-climb paint can make fences difficult to grip and marks anyone who touches it, but pair it with warning signs and follow the product's reapplication instructions closely.

According to recent reports, finally, photograph valuables and record serial numbers in an inventory stored somewhere secure. An ultraviolet pen can add ownership details that aren't normally visible, while a forensic marking kit links items to a unique registered code. Neither will stop a theft, but both can help police identify recovered property and make an insurance claim less painful.

One way to help prevent break-ins is to make your home look occupied even when it's not. Start outside with motion-activated lights at entrances, along driveways and on paths. For a side passage or secluded corner, a dusk-to-dawn light switches on automatically when daylight fades, while a solar model avoids running a cable. Smart bulbs and floodlights can go a step further, with schedules tied to local sunset so they shift automatically as the days get shorter, or by switching on when a camera or sensor detects motion.

In a recent development, aim the light at the approach rather than into a camera lens or a neighbor's window. The goal is to expose movement and give any camera a usable image, not to turn the whole yard into a stadium.

Industry observers note that inside, put a few lamps on timers or smart plugs that switch on around dusk, and vary the schedule if you're away. A smart plug also lets you adjust the lights from your phone if you're delayed getting home or traveling, so the house doesn't sit dark on the one night it matters. Leaving one light on all day can have the opposite effect, because a lamp burning at midday suggests that nobody is there to turn it off.

It's also worth closing curtains or blinds in the evening so screens and valuables aren't visible, and asking a neighbor to collect mail and deliveries.

In a recent development, then there's the use of other smart security devices. The best home security cameras, of course, are a major one. Place cameras around the routes someone would actually use. The front step matters, but so do the side gate and rear entrance. Good lighting on those approaches will usually do more for night footage than a bigger night-vision range claim, because you need enough detail to identify a face at the gate rather than simply spot a shape. Many smart cameras also let you draw activity zones, so you're alerted to someone at the gate but not to every passing car or neighbor, and models with a built-in spotlight or two-way audio let you light up the area or speak to a visitor from your phone.

It has been revealed that the evidence broadly supports that layered approach. A 2019 systematic review of 40 years of research, led by Eric Piza, found that closed-circuit television systems were associated with a significant and modest decrease in crime, with better results when cameras were combined with other measures, so a camera on its own isn't really a perimeter.

It has been revealed that visible alarms still have real value, and in a UNC Charlotte study of 422 convicted burglars, 60% mentioned an alarm would make them choose another target. Monitoring is the part that turns a notification into action. A monitored service watches alerts constantly and can escalate them when you don't respond.

Sources indicate that it's also worth making sure your cameras are charged up properly. The usual advice for battery cameras is to keep a second charged pack to swap in, or add a compatible solar panel or USB-C charger where conditions allow. A solar panel won't perform miracles on a shaded wall in December, of course, so keep in mind where the sun will hit when it is out.

Industry observers note that apart from standard cameras, a smart video doorbell can help too. The front door, of course, is where deliveries and visitors arrive. With a smart doorbell, you can see and talk to them straight from your phone, even when you're not there.

The cheapest useful check is to simply walk around your property at dusk and look at it as a stranger would. Can someone reach the back gate unseen? Are ladders out, valuables visible through a window, or packages sitting on the step?

Industry observers note that start with those basics. Good locks, sensible lighting and a routine for looking occupied come first. Then add monitoring that fits your home, whether that's a visible alarm or a well-placed camera, and extend the same attention to sheds, cars and parcels.

Before you travel, test the alarm sensors, clean the cameras, charge or replace batteries in cameras and smart locks, confirm that auto-lock and your lighting schedules are working, confirm that alerts reach someone who can act on them, and check the policy's unoccupied limit.

You don't need to overhaul everything at once to improve the odds. A locked door, a lit approach and a delivery that isn't sitting outside for six hours go a long way, and a camera or alarm that alerts you when something does happen makes those habits more effective.

Industry News: Microsoft blames monster email outage on software defect introduced in July fix

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (798 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Theregister

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Summer code change caused a Fall fail – frantic engineers had to patch the patch instead of rolling back.
  • Microsoft has blamed last week's epic outage on a change it made in July that lurked in the network gateway servers until a surge in load and a drop in capacity triggered the defect, giving the Microsoft 365 world a day off from email.
  • According to a preliminary post incident report published by Microsoft on November 15, the defect was introduced in July 2026.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Summer code change caused a Fall fail – frantic engineers had to patch the patch instead of rolling back.

Microsoft has blamed last week's epic outage on a change it made in July that lurked in the network gateway servers until a surge in load and a drop in capacity triggered the defect, giving the Microsoft 365 world a day off from email.

According to a preliminary post incident report published by Microsoft on November 15, the defect was introduced in July 2026. The upgrade looked fine at the time, Microsoft says, having passed load testing and been deployed without any impact.

Sources indicate that however, the testing wasn't good enough. Microsoft's report states: "Our load testing tended to focus on weaker hardware with fewer cores." The defect caused "lock contention inside an internal Windows process which caused the machine's resources (CPU & memory) to be exhausted.".

"The contention issue is worsened on machines with more cores and newer hardware.".

Industry observers note that the fix containing the defect was prepared specifically for Microsoft 365 network gateway servers. Then two things happened at once. Teams failed over to the "primary" gateway that supports Exchange Online, creating a surge in load that was not, in itself, particularly unusual. At the same time, almost 14 percent of server capacity for the networking gateway was out of service, which wasn't a problem by itself either: it was on its way to being restored and, according to Microsoft, "the service had sufficient capacity headroom." Together, they pushed the gateway into the defect and chaos ensued.

It was a classic cascading failure scenario. When a server loses connectivity, traffic gets routed to the next healthy endpoint. Which encountered the same problem. So traffic was rerouted again and… you can see where this was going. Within two hours, the defect was encountered across Microsoft's fleet. "At its lowest," the report states, "more than 80 percent of servers were unresponsive.".

It has been revealed that so, what to do? Bringing servers back to service didn't help – they were immediately overwhelmed and fell over again.

"Our normally automated recovery processes were not designed to restore service from this broad unresponsive state." A straightforward rollback was also not possible because the defect was months old.

Instead, engineers developed patch for the patch or, in Microsoft's words, "an upgrade that returned the code path to the previously known good state in Windows." The patch was applied to groups of servers and service was gradually restored.

The timings show the pain customers experienced and the floundering in Redmond as Microsoft tried to work out why Exchange Online and other cloud services were so poorly. The Teams failover, which turned out to be a factor in the outage, happened at 0107 UTC on November 12. During the day, the load began to ramp up until, at 1603 UTC, Microsoft's connectivity anomaly detection monitor identified an increase in connectivity issues.

At 1633 UTC, the first support case came in.

Recent findings suggest that it is not difficult to imagine the stress engineers felt as, over the next 15 hours, nothing they tried resolved the issue. All ongoing and planned deployments and configuration changes were paused while the team attempted to resurrect the service. Extra capacity was added. Traffic was rerouted. Yet servers kept falling over.

"Those services that were able – like Teams, OneDrive, SharePoint, and Office apps – failed out of the faulty network gateway infrastructure," the report claims. "But not all services, like Exchange Online, can fail out of this network gateway for scale reasons.".

Hence the length of time for which Exchange Online (or, from the perspective of many users, Outlook) was out of action.

By 0030 UTC on November 13, Microsoft had identified connection negotiation as the main culprit for the access failures and concluded that competing processes were preventing connections from being handled.

However, it took until 0720 UTC before "We identified a mitigation and applied the mitigation –  an update that reverted the defective change.".

At 1610 UTC, Microsoft confirmed that things were once again looking healthy and, at 0415 on November 14, issued its final customer enhancement.

A final post incident report is due on November 20. However, the preliminary report will do little to calm jangling nerves. An update applied three months ago managed to cause Exchange Online (and other services) disruption on a global scale? With load testing that didn't reflect scenarios under Microsoft's control?

The engineers who worked feverishly to restore services deserve commendation and will hopefully never have to buy their own beverages in Redmond again (or at least escape the next round of firings). However, the processes that led to an enhancement with a latent defect reaching production deserve a long, hard look. ®.

According to recent reports, following the news of the nomination, Cyrus took to social media to reflect on the moment. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, if you were having trouble accessing certain services like Microsoft Teams or Outlook, you were not alone. Early Thursday afternoon, many of Microsoft's biggest apps and services were experiencing downtime. According to Downdetector, which tracks user reports of problems with websites and platforms, Microsoft 365, Teams, Copilot, Teams, and OneDrive were all experiencing issues. As of Friday afternoon, Microsoft has restored service to many users, and has officially apologized for the outages.

According to recent reports, when I first published this article on Thursday, I couldn't even load Microsoft 365's status page. (I've reported on many service outages, but I can't recall a time when a service's status page was also down.) Even as of Friday afternoon, the page still indicates "Service degradation on Microsoft 365 (Business or Enterprise)," and Microsoft says the following services may be affected: Exchange Online, Microsoft 365 admin center, Microsoft 365 apps, Microsoft 365 Apps Admin Center, Microsoft 365 Education, Microsoft Copilot 365, Microsoft Defender for Office 365, Microsoft Defender XDR, Microsoft Fabric, Microsoft Graph, Microsoft Intune, Microsoft Planner, Microsoft Power Apps, Microsoft Purview, Microsoft Teams, Microsoft To Do, Power BI, SharePoint Online, Universal Print, and Windows 365.

Looking specifically at Outlook, Microsoft's email service had hundreds of thousands of user reports Thursday afternoon, signaling a major issue somewhere in Microsoft's pipeline. The reports did "slow down" throughout the day, but Downdetector still showed over 50,000 reports coming in every 15 minutes when I checked Thursday afternoon.

Industry observers note that while the root cause of the concern was a mystery throughout Thursday's outage, Microsoft confirmed the problem in an apology on Friday. According to the company, "This was a technical issue not related to cyber or AI [or] agents. The incident was introduced by an issue during an earlier network capacity upgrade that surfaced following a recent network change. We have addressed the underlying issue and continue to restore service to remaining customers and regions.".

Industry observers note that microsoft claims it is "deeply sorry" for the disruption to its customers and partners. The company says the fix rolled out slower than some might expect, since it wanted to restore service gradually to evaluate stability at each stage. It also says it will release a full post-incident report once it completes a review.

According to recent reports, during the outage, the organization had confirmed that some of its infrastructure was experiencing elevated load, which it remarked was likely contributing to the issues. Microsoft then said it was pausing all deployments and moving traffic from affected infrastructure, and that it found that a number of its servers were unexpectedly unavailable after failing health checks. The company then thought a specific component responsible for processing server health may be the reason the system is failing health checks. Microsoft said an alternative service health check method successfully restarted some of the affected servers. The company was then actively restarting and validating affected servers to bring them back to service.

#16311. Five essential steps to protect your holiday packages from porch pirates

📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 10m • 📚 Deep Dive (1925 w)

Five essential steps to protect your holiday packages from porch pirates

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (1925 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Tomsguide

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Porch piracy is still a major problem.
  • Of course, there are things you can and should do to keep your packages safe.
  • Sources indicate that if you're looking for a deal on a video doorbell this Black Friday, the crystal-clear 2K video on Arlo's option helps you keep an eye out for holiday deliveries and feel connected to your home, even when you're away.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Porch piracy is still a major problem. 30% of American adults have had a package stolen at some point in their lives, and 49% worry more about package theft during the holidays than at other times of year, according to Security.org’s 2026 Package Theft Report. The report estimates that 47.7 million people had a package stolen in the past year, and that the stolen packages were worth $7.7 billion. And with the average adult expecting 28 deliveries between October and December, there’s simply plenty more opportunity for boxes to sit unattended.

Of course, there are things you can and should do to keep your packages safe. The best protections stop a theft before the package lands, either by arranging a verified hand-off, shortening the time a box spends outside, or sending it somewhere secure. Here are some practical ways to protect your packages from porch pirates this holiday season.

Sources indicate that if you're looking for a deal on a video doorbell this Black Friday, the crystal-clear 2K video on Arlo's option helps you keep an eye out for holiday deliveries and feel connected to your home, even when you're away. Arlo Chime 2 offers convenient in-home audio notifications, while the Arlo Secure App provides real-time, personalized notifications and the ability to see and talk with visitors on your doorstep.

The strongest option for an expensive order is probably to require a verified hand-off. UPS Protected Delivery, which launches Nov. 16, requires the recipient to give the driver a PIN, or numeric code, before an eligible package is released. FedEx Authenticated Delivery uses a unique QR code instead. Both of these services are a little limited in how and where you can use them, and they may cost more too. The shipper, not the recipient, has to select either one, so ask the retailer before you order.

Industry observers note that for everything else, the carrier’s tracking app is the first line of defense. Turn on notifications from Amazon, UPS, FedEx and USPS, and act on the “out for delivery” message rather than waiting for “delivered.”.

According to recent reports, security.org identifies delivery alerts as a popular prevention method, with 39% of shoppers using delivery notifications or tracking apps. An alert alone won’t protect a box, but it at least gives you a notification you can act on relatively quickly.

“The goal shouldn’t be watching your front door all day,” says Ken Sedberry, director of Xfinity Shield. “It should be knowing when a package arrives and having a strategy to bring it inside.”.

Recent findings suggest that amazon’s scheduling tools can shorten that exposure further. Map Tracking reveals the driver’s live position on eligible deliveries, while estimated two- to four-hour delivery windows give you something more useful than an all-day estimate. Prime members can also use Amazon Day to batch orders onto one day each week when someone is home. Security.org found that 43% of shoppers schedule deliveries for when someone will be there.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

Photo on Delivery adds a record of where the driver left the package, which is especially helpful if it ended up behind a planter or at a side entrance. It doesn’t prove the package stayed there, though.

For valuable shipments, a traditional signature requirement is still worth requesting if the newer verification services aren’t available. The sender usually has to add it, and fees vary by carrier and service.

The best way to secure where packages are left is to not leave them there in the first place. That may sound silly, but there are actually a few different ways you can prevent packages from being left alone on your doorstep. Amazon Locker and Counter are free alternatives, and they’re part of a network of more than 25,000 pickup locations across the country.

“For those receiving a high volume of deliveries, especially during the holidays, giving carriers a secure place to leave packages is much more effective than simply hoping a camera discourages someone from taking them,” says Rod Sides, founder of Loxx Boxx, which makes package lockboxes.

Recent findings suggest that lockers give you three calendar days to collect a package, and size or item restrictions mean not every order qualifies. Staffed Counters at retailers offer another option if you’d rather collect from a person.

Sources indicate that carriers like UPS and FedEx have their own pickup locations too. UPS Access Point locations hold packages for up to seven days at no charge, although redirecting an in-flight package costs $5.99 for free Basic My Choice members. Premium, at $19.99 a year, includes it. FedEx Hold at Location keeps packages for up to seven days at FedEx Office and FedEx facilities, but FedEx says to pick up within five business days at participating retailers such as Walgreens and Dollar General. Redirecting to a retail location is free.

USPS offers free Hold for Pickup through Delivery Instructions, along with free Hold Mail for three to 30 days when you’re away. Its Smart Lockers in Post Office lobbies provide another free option with a five-day collection window. Hold windows and redirect fees change periodically, so confirm them in the carrier’s app before rerouting a valuable order.

It has been revealed that home parcel boxes are more convenient, but they depend on driver cooperation. Some allow you to lock packages behind a four-digit PIN — but a driver rushing through deliveries in a busy season may not take the time to do that, or may not see the request in the first place.

Sources indicate that if you do go the route of using a drop box, it's worth anchoring it properly. An empty, lightweight lockbox can be carried away and opened elsewhere, so bolt it down or weight it properly. Then make it as hidden from the street as you can. Delivery instructions should name an exact hiding place rather than simply saying “front door.” Something like “inside the parcel box behind the side gate” gives the driver a workable instruction. It still isn’t a guarantee, and some carrier menus offer limited space for custom directions.

According to recent reports, some of the best home security cameras and video doorbells can help deter porch pirates as well. A battery-powered video doorbell is a pretty reasonable entry-level option. Look for higher-resolution 2K video, a wide-angle view, person and package alerts, and a choice of battery or wired power.

Prices tend to drop during holiday sales, but keep in mind that the hardware price is only part of the cost. Cloud recording, which saves clips to the manufacturer’s servers rather than in your home, typically requires a subscription.

Person and package detection makes these devices much easier to live with. AI, in this context, mostly means pattern-recognition software that distinguishes people and packages from other movement. It reduces alerts caused by passing cars, animals or swaying branches. It can make a pretty big difference.

“Delivery drivers often drop a package without ringing the bell, but a motion alert lets you know the moment someone is at your door, often before the carrier’s delivery email arrives, so you don’t have to keep watching the front door,” says Veronica Moturi, senior vice president and chief customer officer at Brinks Home.

It's worth keeping in mind the fact that cameras don't always deter theft and often document it more than prevent it. Pairing one with motion-activated lighting and a camera monitoring sign can help with the deterrence, though.

According to recent reports, lighting deserves special attention during the winter, when many deliveries arrive after dark. A lit entrance helps drivers find the right drop spot and removes some of the cover a thief would prefer.

“Look for a camera with clear night vision, since shorter days mean more deliveries and holiday visits happen after dark,” says Moturi.

Recent findings suggest that apartment residents have a lot more reason to proposal ahead. Security.org found that 10% of apartment dwellers had a package stolen in the previous three months, compared with 3% of single-family home residents. That’s more than three times as likely. Shared lobbies, dense delivery traffic and long periods with nobody watching the entrance all create opportunities.

Recent findings suggest that if your apartment building offers some kind of locked package room or front desk, it may be worth having packages left there rather than in front of your door. If you don't, there's no harm in requesting one from building management — and if there have been thefts, a request from multiple tenants could carry more weight.

In a recent development, renting also makes it harder to mount security cameras and smart doorbells. Thankfully, there are plenty of battery-operated ones that don't require drilling or changing wiring, so if you are renting and want something like that, they are available.

Sources indicate that if you do fall victim to a porch pirate, there are a few things to do. Start by verifying that the package is actually missing. Check the tracking status and delivery photo, then ask household members, neighbors or the doorman whether they collected it. Look around side entrances and other plausible drop spots. Sometimes, you might find that it wasn't stolen at all.

If you still can't find it, it's worth contacting the retailer promptly with the order number, tracking details, delivery date and any photos or footage you have. That’s usually the fastest route to a replacement before a holiday.

According to recent reports, amazon often asks customers to wait about 48 hours after a package is marked delivered and to file a missing-package claim within 30 days of the delivery date, but policies differ for third-party sellers and other retailers. Refunds and replacements are common, not guaranteed.

According to recent reports, file a police report even if the retailer refunds you or sends a replacement. Only 23% of recent victims in Security.org’s survey reported their most recent theft to police. Those reports really help departments identify repeat locations, spot organized activity and decide where to assign patrols.

Recent findings suggest that purchase protection through a card such as American Express may cover eligible items for 90 days after purchase, and Amex asks for notice of a claim within 30 days of the loss or as soon as reasonably possible. Terms vary, so you’ll want to check your benefits before relying on them.

In a recent development, gene Petrino, a former SWAT commander and police sergeant, offers the simplest summary of the whole problem. “Thieves can’t steal what they can’t see.”.

In a recent development, concealment matters, but removing the package from public view altogether is better. No single gadget covers every delivery, and paid verification won’t be available for every order. The best proposal to protect your packages is to combine methods. Do what you can to prevent them from being left alone in the first place, use carrier alerts to get your packages to safety quickly, and use security cameras as a deterrent or to monitor anything that does get stolen.

Christian de Looper is a freelance writer who has covered every facet of consumer tech, including mobile, audio, home theater, computing, gaming, and even car tech. #16309. Industry News: I Used AI to Fake a Scientific Paper. Here’s What Happened
